LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights How to watch as these two teams take center stage on "Thursday Night Football" after Week 7 losses IMAGN Images via Reuters Connect In the Week 8 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Green Bay Packers play host to the Carolina Panthers . The Packers enter this game off a disappointing loss to the division rival Detroit Lions , in a game they had multiple chances to win. Green Bay had won three in a row to salvage its season after a blowout loss to the Atlanta Falcons the last time the Packers played on Thursday night (Week 3), but they hit a bump in the road last week. Now, they're looking to make it four wins in five games. The Panthers are coming off an embarrassing blowout loss at the hands of the division rival Tampa Bay Buccaneers . Carolina was blasted 43-13 last week and was never truly competitive, falling down 17-0 early. However, the Panthers still sit at .500 after climbing that hump with their win over the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 6. Now, they try to get back to their winning ways. Which of these two teams will get back in the win column? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Packers vs. Panthers live Date: Thursday, Oct. 29 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Lambeau Field (Green Bay) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Packers -3/5, O/U 47.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Panthers have the ball The Panthers limped to their worst offensive performance of the season last week, managing just 266 yards, 15 first downs and 13 points while turning the ball over four times. They had previously gained at least 340 yards in every game, gained at least 24 first downs in four of five, and scored 25-plus points in four of five. Bryce Young returned to poor form on Sunday, going only 14-of-27 for 163 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions, while also fumbling once. He's now completed south of 52% of his passes in back-to-back games and south of 55% in three of his last four, with the only exception being a game against the decrepit Lions pass defense. Young got off to a hot start to the season , but he's cooled off a bit as of late. The Packers have been a tough matchup for opposing quarterbacks this year. They're eighth in net passing yards per attempt, and they've yet to allow more than 296 net passing yards in any game this season. They've also allowed just nine touchdown passes against nine interceptions. Jonathan Gannon has been good at limiting what opponents can do through the air, for the most part. It is, however, worth noting that the Packers faced Carson Wentz , Geno Smith , Michael Penix Jr. , Jalon Daniels and Tyson Bagent before getting Dak Prescott and Jared Goff over the last two weeks. So they haven't exactly done this against a murderer's row of opponents. Green Bay has gotten pressure at a below-average rate — no surprise with Micah Parsons still sidelined. Instead, the Packers have gotten by against the pass with sticky coverage and timely plays on the ball. Keisean Nixon and Brandon Cisse have been solid on the outside. Javon Bullard has played well in the slot, and the safeties are providing quality help over the top and in the middle of the field. Carolina's passing game is mostly built outside the numbers with Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker , though Young has thrown over the middle more this season than in past years. It'll be up to the skyscrapers on the perimeter to win their one-on-one matchups here in order to give Young room to throw, though he should have more time than he did last week thanks to Green Bay's relatively weaker pass rush. In the run game, the Panthers lean on Chuba Hubbard , who is averaging 4.8 yards per carry in a workhorse role in the absence of Jonathon Brooks . Hubbard only got seven carries in the negative game script last week, but you can likely expect the Panthers to try to "Establish The Run" here as a way to get their offense back on track. Green Bay has allowed only 3.9 yards per carry this season, though, so it might be tough, especially with right tackle Taylor Moton now on the sidelines. When the Packers have the ball The Packers welcomed Josh Jacobs back to the lineup last week but still found themselves entirely unable to run the ball against the Lions. They totaled just 60 yards on the ground, with Jacobs himself carrying 11 times for only 36 yards. Green Bay is now averaging a pathetic 2.9 yards per carry on the season, which unsurprisingly ranks dead last in the league. The Panthers, meanwhile, were run over by the Bucs last week. Bucky Irving and Co. blew past Carolina for a remarkable 258 yards on the ground, which was made all the more incredible by the fact that the Panthers had yielded just 81 rushing yards in their previous two games combined. Still, Carolina has allowed 5.2 yards per carry on the season now, which, to no surprise, ranks dead last. Almost 60% of the rushing yards the Panthers have allowed, though, came in their games against the Bucs and the Chicago Bears in Week 1. They've been fine-ish against the run otherwise. So, can the Packers run the ball with any degree of success here? If the recent history of this season is any indication, then the answer is probably not. Jacobs has been at or below 4.0 yards per carry in two of his last three full seasons, and spending six weeks on the commissioner's exempt list in the wake of a disturbing domestic violence incident probably didn't make him a more efficient runner. And the offensive line is still not a good run-blocking unit. So, the fate of the Packers' offense likely once again falls on the right shoulder of Jordan Love . Love has only completed 59.8% of his passes at an average of 7.4 yards per attempt this season, but he's been victimized by a league-high 21 drops, according to Tru Media. Love is attacking deep downfield consistently, with a 9.1-yard average depth of throw that ranks fourth-highest in the NFL . As such, he's created explosive plays (16-plus-yard gains) at the third-highest rate in the league among 33 qualified quarterbacks. He should see favorable matchups when he looks downfield on Thursday night. Panthers starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson remain out on injured reserve, which has left rookie Will Lee III and Akayleb Evans as the starting corners. But Evans is also out on Thursday night, meaning, well, I honestly don't even know who is going to step up in his absence. The Panthers elevated Marco Wilson from the practice squad, and they may need to shift Chau Smith-Wade outside. Either way, it's not a great situation for Carolina. Christian Watson and Matthew Golden , who is trending to play, should be able to find space down the field against these corners, and then it's just a matter of actually hanging onto the ball when Love puts it on them. Green Bay could have a big night through the air if the Packers can protect Love, which will be made easier by the absence of Panthers edge rusher Jaelan Phillips , who is also out for this game. It was surprising to see the Panthers get smacked in the face by the Buccaneers last week. The Packers probably can't do the same thing the Bucs did — run the ball down Carolina's throat — but they can still beat that defense with explosive plays. With the top two cornerbacks still out, Watson and Golden (if he plays) are going to be able to find space in the defense. Green Bay's own defense has also played better as of late after a rough start to the season. Green Bay is set as a 3.5-point favorite at home in this primetime matchup, and it’s looking to stay over .500 in the 2026 season after a Week 7 loss to Detroit. Despite a three-game winning streak earlier this season and a 4-3 record overall, the Packers are in last place in the NFC North heading into Week 8. So, every game means a ton for Jordan Love, Matt LaFleur and Co. as they look to get back to the playoffs. Bryce Young and the Panthers are in a different spot, as they’re in first place in the weak NFC South despite going 3-3 through their first six games. Carolina lost at home to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 7, and it only has a half-game lead over the Atlanta Falcons in the division. The Panthers won the NFC South last season, but a litany of injuries to open the 2026 campaign have put them in a tough spot to repeat. Still, oddsmakers aren’t expecting them to have another blowout loss with this spread set inside a touchdown on Thursday. All week long, the SI Betting team has shared our favorite game picks, props, anytime touchdown scorer selections and more for Panthers vs. Packers. Here’s a quick look at some of our favorites to give our readers a one-stop shop to prepare for Thursday Night Football. The Packers' defense ranks 12th in opponent EPA per play and 10th in opponent EPA per dropback, so with them being on their home field on a short week, I expect them to get to Young in this game. I'll take the Packers to cover on Thursday Night Football. Packers running back Josh Jacobs missed the first six weeks of the season on the Commissioner's Exempt List, but he returned in Week 7 and made an immediate impact against the Detroit Lions. Jacobs played just 52.2 percent of Green Bay’s offense snaps, but he saw 18 opportunities (11 rushes, seven targets) and ended up finding the end zone. The former first-round pick had 11 carries for 36 yards and caught five of his seven targets for 55 yards (and a receiving score) in the loss to Detroit. He has a great matchup against a Carolina defense that is 30th in EPA/Rush, 32nd in yards per carry allowed and 32nd in rushing touchdowns allowed (11) this season. While this isn’t the most favorable price, Jacobs has been a touchdown machine in his Packers career, scoring 31 times in 33 games. He’s an easy bet against one of the worst run defenses in the NFL. Bryce Young has been one of the best passers in the NFL even with his rough showing in Week 7 against Tampa Bay. In six games, Young has thrown for 1,712 yards and 12 scores, reaching at least 281 passing yards in five of his six games. He’s also posted four games with multiple touchdown passes. Green Bay is fifth in the NFL in EPA/Pass, but the Lions showed in Week 7 that you can throw on this team by attacking the outside corners. They lined Amon-Ra St. Brown – usually their slot receiver – outside quite a bit, and he finished the day 153 receiving yards. Plus, deep-ball threat Jameson Williams had two scores and 91 yards in the win. So, I expect Young and the Panthers to air it out against Green Bay, which has still allowed nine passing scores this season. Young has 36 or more pass attempts in five of his six games, so I think he’s a strong bounce-back candidate after a weird Week 7 game got out of hand very quickly for Carolina. Love has thrown the ball quite a bit in the 2026 season, and former first-round pick Matthew Golden has been one of the biggest beneficiaries. Through seven games, Golden has 69 targets, 36 catches and 540 receiving yards. He’s also found the end zone three times. Now, Love and Golden haven’t connected as much as you’d expect given his target share, but the second-year wideout still has five games with at least five receptions. Golden also has six or more targets in every game and four games with 12 or more looks. So, the volume should be there against a Carolina defense that is pretty average against the pass (13th in EPA/Pass) this season. I think Golden is undervalued at this number in Week 8. picks.blurb: Predictions: Will Packers Score Thursday Night Bounce-Back vs. Panthers? It couldn’t possibly go worse than when they lost to the Falcons 35-14 on Thursday night last month. “Yeah, I should change everything, huh?” defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon sort-of joked on Wednesday, “because we laid an egg – me I’m talking about. I hold that to ourselves. I think Matt (LaFleur) made some tweaks, which I really liked. I think it’s going to help our guys. We’ll see, the proof will be in the pudding.” The Packers need to find a victory in the pudding against Carolina. Green Bay is in last place in the NFC North and holds a tenuous grip on the final spot in the NFC. Obviously, it’s early to be overly concerned about the playoff race, but the division race is in danger of getting away from them before the calendar flips to November. Will the Packers win? Here are our weekly predictions. Bill Huber’s Packers-Panthers Prediction The Packers and Panthers are two of the most beat-up teams in the NFL , a fact complicated by playing on a Thursday. The injuries are probably one reason why these also are among the most inconsistent teams in the league. It seems like the Packers have a lot of injuries. But is that true? Here's some good injury data shared by @RotoWire . ⬇️ https://t.co/Mp2IlrCeZW The Packers can’t get out of their own way on offense, which is why they’ve scored 20 or fewer points in four of seven games. They scored only 17 points last week against the Lions, who have one of the worst defenses in the NFL. Detroit entered the game on pace to blow away the dubious league record for passing yards allowed. Jordan Love and Co. failed miserably to capitalize, especially in key moments. The Panthers are no better. Remember Green Bay’s loss to Atlanta at Lambeau? That came just days after Carolina went into Atlanta and won by 31. The Panthers had won three of their last four games until getting steamrolled 43-13 by the Buccaneers. So, which team(s) will show up tonight? So, let’s bring it back to injuries. The Panthers’ starting cornerbacks, Mike Jackson and Jaycee Horn, are on injured reserve. Their best pass rusher, Jaelan Phillips, will be inactive due to injury. So, there should be opportunities for the Packers to make plays in the passing game. Combined with a matchup against the worst run defense in the NFL, this could be a breakout game for Green Bay’s offense. “Should be,” of course, is the operative phrase. The only thing the Packers do consistently is play inconsistently. They can’t run the football. They struggle to protect the passer. They drop passes. They misfire on third down and squander opportunities in the red zone. So, should the Packers have a big game offensively? Yes. But will they? At least the defense is good, with Gannon earning his paycheck by fielding a formidable unit that has mostly played winning football even though it can’t rush the passer with a traditional four-man rush. So, who wins? I’d give the advantages to Green Bay on both sides of the ball. On offense, Love should have a strong game against Carolina’s depleted pass defense. Heck, they might even be able to run the football against the league’s worst rush defense. On defense, the Packers have spoken highly of Panthers quarterback Bryce Young all week, but Young is not as good as Detroit’s Jared Goff and the Panthers have only one big-time threat in the passing game compared to two for Detroit. The Panthers will be without their preferred starting offensive tackles, too. So, the Packers will score a key win. A 5-3 start with Micah Parsons still not back on the practice field would be a major victory for a team that has aspirations to be playing deep into January. Bill’s Prediction: Packers 27, Panthers 17. Bill’s Record: 5-2. Here are the 10 most important Packers for tonight's game, a story filled with quotes and other good stuff by @JacobWestendorf . ⬇️ https://t.co/tX2pc7MrfW Jacob Westendorf’s Packers-Panthers Prediction I don't think this game is going to be pretty. Matt LaFleur said earlier this week that Panthers coordinator Ejiro Evero's defense forces everyone on offense to be consistent on every single play. The Packers have not been like that all season. The injuries on the offensive line make for some uncertainty, and give this coaching staff a chance to screw up the starting five combination, like they have so many times in the past. Meanwhile, the Panthers (3-3) are in first place in the NFC South despite a major blowout loss at home against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday. Ekwonu is expected back in the next month or so. CHARLOTTE, N.C. (AP) — The Carolina Panthers are probably wishing they could petition the NFL for another bye week. Mounting injuries to the secondary and offensive line have begun to take their toll on the Panthers (3-4), who have dropped two straight games and fallen into a tie with the Atlanta Falcons for first place in the NFC South. On Friday, the Panthers fired defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero after the team allowed Jordan Love to throw for 288 yards and three touchdowns in a 27-19 loss to the Green Bay Packers. Carolina entered the game last in the league in run defense. The Panthers promoted defensive line coach Todd Wash as interim defensive coordinator. Evero's fate may have been sealed when starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson went down in a Week 3 loss to the Cleveland Browns and were placed on injured reserve. Since then, the two cornerbacks who were replaced Horn and Jackson have suffered injuries. Akayleb Evans was placed on IR last week and Will Lee injured his hamstring against the Packers in the first half and had to leave the game. Canales said the injuries were taken into account when he fired Evero, but added that the decision was based on the big picture and “a lot of information." Things are just as shaky on the offensive line where the Panthers are playing without three starters, including tackles Taylor Moton and Ickey Ekwonu and guard Damien Lewis. Bryce Young was under constant pressure against the Packers. He was hurried 22 times, hit nine times and sacked six times. “We’ve got to make sure we do a good job of giving him solutions when they do have overloaded pressures and zero looks and things," Canales said. "But it wasn’t just that. They got after us with some four-man rushes and some stunts that we didn’t pass off well. That created a little bit of pressure there as well.” Rookie first-round pick Monroe Freeling has struggled at right tackle this season. Hubbard was used extensively against the Packers and gained 81 yards on 22 carries while hauling in a team-high seven passes for 38 yards. He's clearly the only back offensive coordinator Brad Idzik trusts at this point in the season. The Minnesota Vikings are the only remaining undefeated team in the NFL, as the San Francisco 49ers were handed their first loss by the Atlanta Falcons , while the Kansas City Chiefs took their first "L" to the Seattle Seahawks . The Vikings have a massive matchup this week, as they take on the high-flying Lions in Detroit. Elsewhere around the NFL , Lamar Jackson looks to make his return to the field against Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills , the Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers face off for the second time in the last month, and the Chicago Bears travel out west to play Sam Darnold and the Seahawks. Which teams should you pick in Week 8, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 27 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) (TNF) Dajani ( Packers -3.5): I'm willing to overlook the Carolina Panthers ' surprising 43-13 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . They are a better team than what they showed last Sunday, but it's difficult to overlook the fact that Carolina's rushing defense ranks dead last in the NFL with 153.2 yards allowed per game. Josh Jacobs rushed for just 36 yards on 11 carries last week against the Lions in his 2026 debut, but I think he's in for a massive homecoming in primetime on a short week. I'm not saying the Packers run away with this one, but I'll take them to cover 3.5 points. … Prediction: Packers 27, Panthers 23 Dubin (Packers -3.5): It was surprising to see the Panthers get smacked in the face by the Buccaneers last week. The Packers probably can't do the same thing the Bucs did — run the ball down Carolina's throat — but they can still beat that defense with explosive plays. With the top two cornerbacks still out, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden (if he plays) are going to be able to find space in the defense. Green Bay's own defense has also played better of late after a rough start to the season. … Prediction: Packers 24, Panthers 17 Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Dajani ( Ravens +3.5): Ignore that Baltimore allowed 35 unanswered points to the Cincinnati Bengals last week, because it appears that Lamar Jackson is back! He was playing some legitimate MVP-level ball before getting hurt, as Jackson went 3-1 as the starter, while completing 70.8% of his passes with 10.1 yards per attempt, six passing touchdowns and just one interception. Only four quarterbacks have put up those kinds of numbers in their first four starts of a season in the past 40 years. The Ravens are a completely different team with Jackson under center, and this Bills defense allows too many points. Buffalo ranks third-worst in scoring defense (28.5 ppg), and has allowed at least 30 points in four of its five victories this season. Jackson is 10-5 SU and 13-2 ATS as an underdog in his career. He's statistically the best quarterback to bet on when listed as an underdog since 1970. … Prediction: Ravens 30, Bills 28 Dubin (Ravens +3.5): This is the same deal as with the Ravens and me pretty much every week: flip the pick if Lamar Jackson sits out again. Otherwise, I like the Ravens to at least keep things close against the Bills. Both of these offenses have been pretty excellent, and the Ravens have been especially so when Jackson has been on the field with Zay Flowers . Ultimately, though, the Bills' home-field advantage and the weaknesses in Baltimore's own pass defense lead me to take the Bills to win and the Ravens to cover. … Prediction: Bills 30, Ravens 27 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) Dajani (Lions -3): I'm shocked by this line, honestly. The only remaining undefeated team in the NFL is a three-point underdog to a division rival? With that said, I think I agree with it. The Vikings' defense is the main reason they are 5-0, as they've allowed a league-leading 12.3 points per game, plus registered a league-leading 10.6% sack rate and 47.6% pressure rate. Offensively, the Vikings have the fewest touchdowns (10) by a 6-0 team since the 1934 Lions and rank 31st in offensive EPA. They could have lost last week to the Indianapolis Colts , who are in the midst of a fire sale. As for the Lions, the concern has always been with their defense. But I think Kelvin Sheppard 's unit is coming along. They allowed just 17 points to the Packers last week, and Brian Branch is back in the lineup. Maybe we could see a push here, but I'm taking the Lions to win … Prediction: Lions 24, Vikings 20 Dubin (Lions -3): Detroit has recently been thrown off its offensive game by Brian Flores' defense, but the offense is operating at an extremely high level right now, with Jared Goff playing as well as he has in recent memory. And as Dajani said, this Minnesota offense just does not have the ability to get into a high-scoring game and come away with a win. They need the defense to hold the opponent down entirely, and I'm not sure that even Flores' bunch can do that in the friendly confines of Ford Field. … Prediction: Lions 23, Vikings 14 Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) Dajani (Steelers -3.5): How can the Browns keep getting away with this? They overcame a 14-0 deficit in Nashville on Sunday, as Harold Fannin Jr . took a short reception 36 yards down the field with 20 seconds remaining to set up a 32-yard game-winning field goal from Andre Szmyt . Deshaun Watson became the third quarterback since 1970 to register a game-winning drive in each of his team's first five wins of the season. With this being a divisional game against an opponent that just got back from Paris, I can understand why some would take the points with the underdog given the hook. But the Steelers are 3-0 ATS at home. That includes Week 3, when they dropped 30 points on Joe Burrow and the Bengals in a win, and Week 5, when Pittsburgh scored 34 points in a double-digit victory over the Colts. Both of these AFC teams are contenders to win the Super Bowl this season, and the Ravens are expected to get Lamar Jackson back in action after he missed three games with a sprained ankle. The Ravens won just one of the three games that Jackson missed, and their offense has struggled over the last two weeks in losses against AFC North opponents in Cleveland and Cincinnati. The Ravens don't want to fall back to .500 this season, and they're set as small underdogs on the road against Buffalo. With every team in the AFC North sitting at over .500 this season, the Ravens can't afford too many more losses, especially against teams that they may be competing for a wild card spot against. Right now, the Bills are in first place in the AFC East, and they're coming off their bye week after a 5-1 start to the season. Josh Allen is the leading candidate to win the MVP award, and he's been terrific as both a passer and a runner. Now, he takes on a Baltimore defense that features Kyle Hamilton, Marlon Humphrey, Nate Wiggins and others in the secondary that could make it tough on a Buffalo passing game that has been short-handed at receiver for a lot of the season. The Bills are hoping to keep things rolling out of their bye, as they're two games up in the loss column on the New England Patriots in the AFC East. Oddsmakers have set Buffalo as a favorite at home, and there are several players on both of these teams that are worth a look in the prop market. So, ahead of this marquee matchup, the SI Betting team has made player prop picks, game picks, anytime touchdown scorer selections and more to help you wager on Bills vs. Ravens. The betting line indicates that he will, so I'm going to trust that, along with the reports that Jesse Minter is optimistic that Jackson will be ready to go. When a team only has one loss on their schedule, and they have the best quarterback in football on their roster, a lot of their issues are overlooked. That's the case for the Bills, whose defense has been horrendous this season, ranking 30th in both opponent EPA per play and opponent success rate. They are the only defense in football that ranks in the bottom three in both of those metrics. I hesitate to lay more than a field goal on any team with that bad of a defense, especially when that defense potentially has to face another MVP candidate at quarterback. I'll take the points with Baltimore on Sunday. Allen has been awesome on the ground this season, carrying the ball 48 times (eight times per game) for 240 yards and eight scores. Allen is the preferred option for the Bills in short yardage, handling eight or more carries in three of his six games. Fresh out of a bye, I expect Allen to be as healthy as he’s been this season, which could be a good sign for him using his legs. The Ravens are allowing over four yards per carry to opposing quarterbacks, and Allen had 14 carries in the meeting between these teams during the 2025 regular season. Baltimore ranks 12th in the league in EPA/Rush, so the Bills and Joe Brady may get creative with the running game rather than riding James Cook (who has had fumbling issues) on Sunday. At plus money, this prop is worth a shot for the former league MVP. Ravens star Zay Flowers has been one of the best receivers in the NFL this season, catching 40 of his 53 targets (in six games) for 608 yards and three scores. Flowers has three games with double-digit targets, and he’s by far the No. 1 option in this passing game. Now, with Jackson expected to return, Flowers should get a major boost against a defense that has not been able to guard anyone in the passing game. After all, the Bills are dead last in the league in EPA/Play on defense. Buffalo’s pass defense is one of the worst in the league, ranking 29th in EPA/Pass while allowing 15 passing scores. Opposing wide receivers have torched the Bills, scoring 11 touchdowns across six games – the most allowed to the position in the NFL. It doesn’t get much better for Flowers, who is averaging over 100 yards per game and has caught at least five passes in every matchup. Since these teams combined for 81 points the last time they played, I’d expect another up-and-down matchup with a ton of offensive possessions for both sides. Flowers has simply been too effective in space, and he has the fourth-highest target share in the NFL this season. That puts him in a great spot to find the end zone for the second week in a row on Sunday. Ravens rookie Ja’Kobi Lane has played just one game with Lamar Jackson, catching one of his three targets in Week 1 against the Indianapolis Colts for 11 yards. The third-round pick missed time with a wrist injury, but he’s returned to play a major role in this offense the last two weeks. Lane played 54.4 percent of the team’s snaps in Week 6 and 68.7 percent of the snaps in Week 7, receiving five targets in each game. He reeled in seven of those passes for 65 yards. While those aren’t huge numbers, Lane has cleared this prop in back-to-back games, and he saw three targets in limited snaps in the opener before going down. Jackson is an immediate boost to Baltimore’s passing offense, so I think Lane is a great bet to clear this prop for the third game in a row, especially if his snap share continues to rise. Oddsmakers are expecting this to be a high-scoring game, even though it's Lamar Jackson's first game back after a three-game absence due to an ankle injury. The total in this matchup is all the way up at 54.5, and it's worth noting that the last time these teams met in the regular season, they combined for 81 points. There are a ton of awesome playmakers in this game, including Derrick Henry, James Cook, Zay Flowers, Dalton Kincaid, DJ Moore and others that could make an impact by scoring a touchdown. So, why don't we bet on a few players to do exactly that? The anytime touchdown scorer market is one of the most exciting ways to bet on the NFL, especially when two of the league's top quarterbacks – Jackson and Josh Allen – are facing off. While Henry, Cook, and Allen are all set at minus odds to find the end zone, I've decided to look at three players at plus money that could score in Week 8. Here's a breakdown of the odds for these picks and my analysis ahead of Sunday’s Raves vs/ Bills clash. Best Anytime Touchdown Scorer Picks for Ravens vs. Bills Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Zay Flowers Anytime TD (+165) Ravens star Zay Flowers has been one of the best receivers in the NFL this season, catching 40 of his 53 targets (in six games) for 608 yards and three scores. Flowers has three games with double-digit targets, and he’s by far the No. 1 option in this passing game. Now, with Jackson expected to return, Flowers should get a major boost against a defense that has not been able to guard anyone in the passing game. After all, the Bills are dead last in the league in EPA/Play on defense. Buffalo’s pass defense is one of the worst in the league, ranking 29th in EPA/Pass while allowing 15 passing scores. Opposing wide receivers have torched the Bills, scoring 11 touchdowns across six games – the most allowed to the position in the NFL. It doesn’t get much better for Flowers, who is averaging over 100 yards per game and has caught at least five passes in every matchup. Since these teams combined for 81 points the last time they played, I’d expect another up-and-down matchup with a ton of offensive possessions for both sides. Flowers has simply been too effective in space, and he has the fourth-highest target share in the NFL this season. That puts him in a great spot to find the end zone for the second week in a row on Sunday. Dalton Kincaid Anytime TD (+210) Dalton Kincaid has just one touchdown for the Bills this season (in Week 2), but the Ravens have struggled to defend the opposition, allowing five tight end touchdown receptions in seven games. Kincaid was an afterthought in the Bills’ offense in Weeks 3, 4 and 5, receiving just seven total targets, but Joe Brady made a point of getting him involved in Week 6. The former first-round pick had eight targets, reeling in seven passes for 38 yards. While it wasn’t a huge day for Kincaid, he had a touchdown negated because of a penalty. I’m buying the Bills star in this matchup, especially since the passing offense has run a lot smoother for Buffalo when he’s one of the top options. Ja’Kobi Lane Anytime TD (+320) Third-round pick Ja’Kobi Lane has appeared in just three games for the Ravens this season due to a wrist injury, catching eight of his 13 targets for 76 yards. He’s yet to find the end zone in the NFL, but with Jackson returning, I’m buying the rookie at this price in Week 7. I’ve already mentioned how awful this Buffalo pass defense is, and if the Bills end up selling out to slow down Flowers, Lane is the next-best option. Lane has seen his snap share rise in back-to-back weeks, playing nearly 70 percent of the offensive plays in Week 6. away.headline: Ravens' Lamar Jackson expected to miss rest of season with thumb injury: report
away.blurb: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson is likely to miss the rest of the season after suffering a thumb injury Sunday on his first play since returning from a high ankle sprain, according to NFL insider Ian Rapoport . Jackson missed Baltimore’s final three games in October due to his ankle issue before returning to action for the Ravens’ Week 8 road game against the Buffalo Bills. His comeback was short-lived, however, as the two-time MVP hurt his right thumb early in the first quarter of Sunday’s loss after hitting his hand on Bills linebacker Greg Rousseau’s arm on his follow-through on a pass attempt. Baltimore head coach Jesse Minter announced following the contest that Jackson would undergo surgery and be placed on injured reserve (IR). To make matters worse, Ravens backup signal-caller Tyler Huntley also suffered an injury versus Buffalo, going down with a toe ailment in the first half. Baltimore’s emergency quarterback, undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano, took over and is currently in line to start the Ravens’ “Thursday Night Football” game against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 9. Fagnano finished his NFL debut versus the Bills 10-for-21 with 91 passing yards, no touchdowns and one interception. Jackson has struggled to stay healthy in recent seasons, missing five games apiece during the 2021 and 2022 campaigns and four more contests last season. Baltimore started the year 4-1 and was at the top of the AFC North standings entering Week 6. The Ravens have lost three in a row since then, however, and are now in last place in the division at 4-4. away.headline: Ravens Make Surprise QB Roster Move After Lamar Jackson’s Injury
away.blurb: Ravens Make Surprise QB Roster Move After Lamar Jackson's Injury Unlock the latest Heavy on Ravens news — direct to your inbox. Many questions linger about the Baltimore Ravens after their 36-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills in Week 8, but the biggest one concerns the quarterback position. Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson returned from his ankle injury and threw only one pass before injuring his thumb. After the game, Ravens head coach Jesse Minter announced that Jackson would go on IR and need surgery on his finger. Backup quarterback Tyler Huntley also got hurt in the first half of the Bills game with a toe injury. Huntley is expected to miss some time as well. That leaves undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano to most likely be the starting quarterback in the Ravens' Week 9 Thursday Night Football showdown against the Jacksonville Jaguars . The question is who will be Fagnano's backup. Baltimore Ravens Announce QB Signing After Lamar Jackson Injury The Ravens announced they would sign quarterback Austin Reed to the roster. Reed is coming off a stint in the United Football League with the Dallas Renegades and was in training camp with the Ravens afterward. "Reed spent part of training camp and the preseason with the team, giving him familiarity with the Ravens' playbook and ability to step in if needed. The Ravens have a quick turnaround with a "Thursday Night Football" game against the Jacksonville Jaguars later this week." "Reed was one of the Ravens' feel-good stories of the preseason, the father of twin girls who were born prematurely in 2025. While they were fighting for their lives, Reed led the United Football League in passing with the Dallas Renegades, trying to take care of his family with a career playing football. Reed also has familiarity with Doyle's offense dating back to when he spent the summer of 2025 with the Chicago Bears and Doyle. Reed will likely back up Joe Fagnano, who stepped in for his NFL regular-season debut after Jackson and Huntley went down. During the preseason, Reed completed 6 of 12 passes for 59 yards, 1 touchdown, and 1 interception. He also had a rushing touchdown in his first preseason game with Baltimore after spending just 72 hours with the team. Baltimore Ravens Won't Be Done Adding Quarterbacks to the Team Reports indicate the Ravens are looking to add a quarterback through a trade. They have spoken with the Chicago Bears about backup quarterback Tyson Bagent . Similar to Reed, Bagent was with Doyle last year in Chicago. Bagent knows the offense and has started multiple games. Baltimore has Reed there as insurance to help with the quarterback position this week. If the Ravens can get Bagent, they will have their starter for the rest of the 2026 season. away.headline: Baltimore Ravens lose QBs Jackson and Huntley to injuries, fall in Buffalo 36-10
away.blurb: Updated on: November 1, 2026 / 8:50 PM EST / CBS Baltimore Down to their third-string quarterback, the Baltimore Ravens lost their third straight game Sunday, falling to the Buffalo Bills, 36-10, at Highmark Stadium. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano entered the game after backup Tyler Huntley injured his toe in the second quarter. Starter Lamar Jackson, who missed the previous three games with an ankle sprain, injured his right thumb on his first pass attempt of the game. Ravens' head coach Jesse Minter said after the game that Jackson will need surgery on the thumb , which could be season-ending. "That'll be a surgery deal. He'll go to (injured reserve)," Minter said. "That's a tough deal." Fagnano was intercepted once, lost a fumble and was sacked three times in his NFL debut. He completed 10 of 21 passes for 91 yards. Buffalo scored the game's first 10 points on a 1-yard touchdown run by Josh Allen and a 56-yard field goal by Tyler Bass. Derrick Henry answered with a 2-yard rushing touchdown to cut the Ravens' deficit to 10-7. Bass added two more field goals to give the Bills a 16-7 halftime lead. James Cook extended Buffalo's lead to 23-10 with a 5-yard touchdown run in the third quarter. Allen followed with an 11-yard touchdown pass to former Maryland Terrapin D.J. Moore and a 23-yard touchdown pass to Dalton Kincaid. Allen finished with 289 passing yards, two touchdown passes and an interception. He also rushed for 30 yards and a touchdown. The Ravens (4-4) have little time to regroup, with the Jacksonville Jaguars coming to Baltimore for a Thursday night game.

Especially after last week’s blown two-score lead to the Cleveland Browns, nobody is expecting Robert Saleh’s first team in Nashville to execute a miraculous turnaround. Draft discussions are already becoming relevant, if that tells you anything. Still, the Titans hit the road to face the Cincinnati Bengals this coming Sunday, and it’s a chance for Tennessee to win their second game in three weeks. That’s somehow still an exciting prospect. To preview the matchup, I’ve got one reason the Titans will beat the Bengals, one reason they won’t, and my own prediction for what will actually happen. Let’s start with the former. Will: Titans’ secondary sees massive uptick Two weeks in a row now, Tennessee has forced at least one interception. The Titans have come down with three picks over the last two games, two of which belong to rising offseason pickup Cor’Dale Flott. Tennessee Titans cornerback Cor'dale Flott (18) intercepts Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones (17) on Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026, at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The Bengals score a lot - a lot - of points. TeamRankings has Cincinnati fourth in the NFL in points per game (27.2) and touchdowns per game (3.2). Their passing statistics specifically are top 10 across the board regarding pass play percentage, completion percentage, and pass yards per game. The Bengals score a lot - a lot - of points. TeamRankings has Cincinnati fourth in the NFL in points per game (27.2) and touchdowns per game (3.2). Their passing statistics specifically are top 10 across the board regarding pass play percentage, completion percentage, and pass yards per game. Tennessee is facing one of the best pass-first teams in the NFL. If Saleh's secondary can find consistency beyond the occasional turnover, the Titans would have more than a fair chance to shut down RB Chase Brown on the ground, too. It's much easier to stop Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins in concept than it is on the field, but doing so is the Titans' key to winning this one. Won’t: Titans can't overcome inconsistent Bengals defense The inverse, of course, is if the Titans' offense continues to suffer. The Bengals have proved themselves beatable against "bad" teams - just see their narrow, one-score win over the 1-6 Miami Dolphins two weeks ago. But Cincinnati also just dismantled the Baltimore Ravens last week, 35-13. The through line is that Cincy scored 30+ points in both of those contests; it comes down to the opposing offense's ability to hang in there when Burrow and his crew get hot. Tennessee ranks 31st in both touchdowns and points per game. Almost everywhere the Bengals are in the top 10 through the air, the Titans are in the bottom 10. Cincy has allowed 20+ points in four of their six games this season. If Cam Ward can get back on his feet in any sense of the saying, another 24-point performance like Tennessee had last week could be enough to at least make this one interesting. However, the Titans may need a little more juice than they've seen yet this season from their QB to stay in it. Prediction: Titans lose, 31-20 Ultimately, I have the Titans falling to 1-7 in this one. We've seen a number of trends solidify that this roster has failed to prove their ability to rise beyond. Carnell Tate is the primary receiver in an otherwise underwhelming offense. The defense can force early turnovers, but can't get late stops when it matters - especially when it comes to tackling. Ward has a better second half than his typically abysmal first, but by the time Tennessee tries to get aggressive, it's too late to make a difference. I expect most of, if not all of these notes to be hit in Week 8. I don't think the Titans will lose in a blowout, but on the road against one of the best offenses in the league, this one already looks like too much for Saleh's team. And with Jeffery Simmons swapping his trademark red sleeves for Chicago orange in a deal that has the Bears surging up the Super Bowl odds board , I like the Over even more, considering the Cincinnati Bengals will do the heavy lifting. Simmons was the shining star and identity of the Tennessee Titans defense. His absence up front will drop the Titans even further down the defensive pecking order, which says something when they're already dead last in DVOA at FTN . The Bengals picked apart a very good Ravens stop unit in the second half of last week's win. They finished with 7.0 yards per play and were a perfect 5 for 5 in the red zone, with Joe Burrow and his talented receiving corps finding their stride. The Titans' secondary allows the second-highest completion rate and has been burned by multiple big plays, bleeding the fourth-most passes of 20+ yards entering Week 8. While they haven't given up many passing touchdowns, they haven't faced many QBs on Burrow's level. Titans vs Bengals combo The Bengals do the lion's share of the scoring, but don't discount the Titans. They're playing with pace and face a Bengals defense that still has work to do. Our Week 8 SGP roundup features a Titans vs. Bengals combo as well. Chase Brown finds the end zone to the cheers of fantasy owners everywhere. He faces a watered-down Titans defense that's allowed six scores to running backs. Tee Higgins ' projections call for as many as 91 yards against a Titans secondary giving up explosive plays. Chase Brown anytime touchdown Tee Higgins 70+ receiving yards Titans vs Bengals touchdown scorer: Chase Brown If anyone was happy to see Simmons traded before Week 8, it was Bengals running back Brown. He no longer has to worry about one of the premier run stoppers in the game, facing a Titans red-zone defense now missing its biggest cog. Even when Simmons was in the mix, the Titans had allowed six scores to rival RBs. Brown has only one touchdown in 2026 despite 13 carries and three receptions in the red zone. Due to that drought, we're getting a discount on his anytime touchdown market in Week 8, considering this prop was trading around 60% two games ago. Given the massive spread, the Bengals will be in a run-positive game script in the second half on Sunday, helping boost Brown's TD probabilities. That includes a 44-yard dinger on a broken play with Burrow dodging pressure. TOP PICK Titans vs Bengals prediction: Over 46.5 One of my first plays of Week 8 was taking the Over in this game. And with Jeffery Simmons swapping his trademark red sleeves for Chicago orange in a deal that has the Bears surging up the Super Bowl odds board , I like the Over even more, considering the Cincinnati Bengals will do the heavy lifting. Simmons was the shining star and identity of the Tennessee Titans defense. His absence up front will drop the Titans even further down the defensive pecking order, which says something when they're already dead last in DVOA at FTN . The Bengals picked apart a very good Ravens stop unit in the second half of last week's win. They finished with 7.0 yards per play and were a perfect 5 for 5 in the red zone, with Joe Burrow and his talented receiving corps finding their stride. The Titans' secondary allows the second-highest completion rate and has been burned by multiple big plays, bleeding the fourth-most passes of 20+ yards entering Week 8. While they haven't given up many passing touchdowns, they haven't faced many QBs on Burrow's level. Titans vs Bengals combo The Bengals do the lion's share of the scoring, but don't discount the Titans. They're playing with pace and face a Bengals defense that still has work to do. John Lanfranca Sun, November 1, 2026 at 5:01 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Cincinnati Bengals (4-2) will host the Tennessee Titans (1-6) in Week 8 of the NFL season this afternoon. Kickoff is set for 1:00 p.m. ET from Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati, Ohio. The game will broadcast live on CBS. The Bengals are 13.5-point favorites over the Titans on the spread, with the total set at over/under 45.5 points. Cincinnati is a -950 moneyline favorite to win outright, while Tennessee is a +640 underdog to pull off the upset. Let's get into my Titans vs Bengals predictions and NFL picks for Sunday, November 1. Titans vs Bengals pick: Bengals -13.5 (-110) My Bengals vs. Titans best bet is Cincinnati to cover the spread. Make sure to find the best odds by checking our live NFL odds page. Titans vs Bengals NFL Odds Titans vs Bengals spread : Titans +13.5 (-110), Titans -13.5 (-110) Titans vs Bengals total : over/under 45.5 (-118o / 104u) Titans vs Bengals moneyline : Titans +640, Bengals -950 Titans vs Bengals Preview for NFL Week 8 Tennessee Titans Preview: Life Without Jeffery Simmons Fading the Titans has been a profitable endeavor this year, but they have covered the number in each of their last two road games. I provided the breakdown for their victory on the road in Indianapolis and their road cover as 11-point underdogs in Baltimore back in Week 4. I will not be going back to the well for a third time in this spot against the Bengals as too many factors are working against them. For starters, the Titans traded away their best defensive player this week in Jeffery Simmons and will also be without leading receiver in Carnell Tate. Opposing running backs have averaged four yards per carry against Tennessee with Simmons on the field — that number increases to 4.5 yards per carry on the 35 carries he has not been in the lineup. The Titans' explosive rush rate allowed also increases from 9.8% with Simmons to 14.3% without Simmons on the field. Simmons boasts the fifth-highest pass rush grade this season out of all defensive tackles , per Pro Football Focus. The lack of interior pressure will allow Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow to build upon his red-hot finish to Week 7. Burrow was surgical in the second half versus Baltimore, completing 88% of his passes for an average of 13.8 yards per attempt. Burrow is heating up, as he historically does as the season progresses — and now, he gets a highly exploitable matchup. Tennessee's defense under head coach Robert Saleh ranks 31st in completion percentage allowed and 27th in yards per attempt allowed. The Titans' pressure rate of 30.6% ranks 26th. However, it is even more concerning when looking at the time charted to get those pressures on quarterbacks. The Titans' 2.8 seconds per pressure is the worst in the NFL, and that number is almost certainly going to get worse with the loss of Simmons. If Tennessee is going to make this game competitive, it has to be the doing of Cam Ward. Tony Pollard and the running game were excellent a week ago versus Cleveland, but the Bengals have the most improved run defense in the league. Cincinnati Bengals Preview: Good Spot for Cincy's Defense Al Golden's defense plays with the highest rate of light boxes in alignment, yet still leads the NFL in stuff rate defending running games. Golden can opt to add an extra defender on early downs to stymie Pollard, which will force Ward into long down-and-distance situations. Without their top weapon on the outside in Tate, the Titans lack playmakers to move the chains when they get to third down. Ward and company already struggle in these situations, ranking 27th in third-down conversion rate. The Bengals boast the eighth-best defense per dropback, according to expected points added (EPA). Projecting the Titans' success in this spot becomes extremely difficult when you consider that 43% of all their pass attempts on 2nd-and-8+ and 28% of all attempts on 3rd- or 4th-and-8+ longer were funneled to Tate. The Titans' passing game is facing an uphill battle in overcoming their deficiencies when their running game on standard downs isn't keeping them ahead of schedule. Titans vs Bengals Picks, Betting Analysis Tennessee has a -62 scoring margin in the first half of games this season, which is the worst in the league. The Titans will likely fall behind early and have no choice but to abandon the running game. This further puts the onus of any potential comeback in the hands of Cam Ward. Ward's 27.1 passer rating under pressure and turnover-worthy throw rate nearly doubling his big-time throw rate makes it too difficult to trust him in delivering any chance at a backdoor cover. The Bengals are -6.5 in the 1st half, which is another position worth a look. However, I am more comfortable allowing the full 60 minutes to play out as Ward's game-altering mistake(s) can come at any time. Joe Burrow is heating up at the right time and the Titans do not have the personnel to slow him down. I expect the Bengals to cruise to victory with significant margin. away.headline: Is Titans WR Carnell Tate Playing vs. Bengals? Latest Injury News
away.blurb: The team revealed several absences , with wide receiver Carnell Tate being officially ruled out with a shoulder injury. Cam Ward loses his top target and the Titans offense, which has struggled mightily to score, is facing a tough task against a surging Bengals team. Carnell Tate Officially Out in Week 8 There is really no reason to have Tate on the field unless he is playing at or near 100%. The Titans are already 1-6 and the team has a bye week following the Bengals game. This extra rest should mean Tate is ready to return in Week 10 and look to form some sort of connection with Ward before the season ends. If they cannot do so, or even if they can, Tate may be catching passes from a new quarterback in 2027. Is Titans WR Carnell Tate Playing vs. Bengals? Latest Injury News Unlock the latest Heavy on Titans news — direct to your inbox. The Tennessee Titans need all hands on deck to have a chance to take down the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday. That is why the team's latest injury report is such a crushing blow. Tate has not yet lived up to the hype of being the No. 4 overall pick in the NFL Draft. However, he has done well given the lack of success from Ward in his role running the offense. The rookie has 34 receptions for 413 yards and one touchdown through seven games. For context, Ward only has four total touchdown passes on the season. The 34 connections make Tate his quarterback's top target and his absence will loom large Sunday in Cincinnati. Carnell Tate Tyjae Spears Tommy Townsend. Yet with or without Tate, the Titans are massive underdogs in the game. ESPN shared DraftKings' odds listing the Bengals as 12.5-point favorites. A 1-6 start is not what Robert Saleh and company had in mind at the start of the season. The team is fresh off back-to-back 3-14 seasons, and seems to be headed in that same direction once again. Ward's second season is not going well and the coaching staff refuses to sit him and let him learn. Thus, they are hoping he can play through his issues and improve to at least make the Titans offense a competitive one. Losing Tate for any amount of time makes even scoring touchdowns a tall task for this offense in 2026. The Titans have the second-worst record in football right now, better than only the 0-6 Los Angeles Chargers . This puts both teams in a race to the bottom for the No. 1 pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. That would be an intriguing draft slot for both teams, as the Titans have Ward and the Chargers have Justin Herbert. Would either team take a quarterback? For now, Ward is hoping to shock the entire NFL world on Sunday with a big performance without his top target on the field. home.headline: Is Titans WR Carnell Tate Playing vs. Bengals? Latest Injury News
home.blurb: The team revealed several absences , with wide receiver Carnell Tate being officially ruled out with a shoulder injury. Cam Ward loses his top target and the Titans offense, which has struggled mightily to score, is facing a tough task against a surging Bengals team. Carnell Tate Officially Out in Week 8 There is really no reason to have Tate on the field unless he is playing at or near 100%. The Titans are already 1-6 and the team has a bye week following the Bengals game. This extra rest should mean Tate is ready to return in Week 10 and look to form some sort of connection with Ward before the season ends. If they cannot do so, or even if they can, Tate may be catching passes from a new quarterback in 2027. Is Titans WR Carnell Tate Playing vs. Bengals? Latest Injury News Unlock the latest Heavy on Titans news — direct to your inbox. The Tennessee Titans need all hands on deck to have a chance to take down the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday. That is why the team's latest injury report is such a crushing blow. Tate has not yet lived up to the hype of being the No. 4 overall pick in the NFL Draft. However, he has done well given the lack of success from Ward in his role running the offense. The rookie has 34 receptions for 413 yards and one touchdown through seven games. For context, Ward only has four total touchdown passes on the season. The 34 connections make Tate his quarterback's top target and his absence will loom large Sunday in Cincinnati. Carnell Tate Tyjae Spears Tommy Townsend. Yet with or without Tate, the Titans are massive underdogs in the game. ESPN shared DraftKings' odds listing the Bengals as 12.5-point favorites. A 1-6 start is not what Robert Saleh and company had in mind at the start of the season. The team is fresh off back-to-back 3-14 seasons, and seems to be headed in that same direction once again. Ward's second season is not going well and the coaching staff refuses to sit him and let him learn. Thus, they are hoping he can play through his issues and improve to at least make the Titans offense a competitive one. Losing Tate for any amount of time makes even scoring touchdowns a tall task for this offense in 2026. The Titans have the second-worst record in football right now, better than only the 0-6 Los Angeles Chargers . This puts both teams in a race to the bottom for the No. 1 pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. That would be an intriguing draft slot for both teams, as the Titans have Ward and the Chargers have Justin Herbert. Would either team take a quarterback? For now, Ward is hoping to shock the entire NFL world on Sunday with a big performance without his top target on the field. A short week isn't typically a good thing, but after snapping a two-game skid, Dallas is chomping at the bit to get back on the field, especially with its explosive offense coming back to life. Here are my best NFL picks for Sunday, Nov. 1, with kickoff set for 1 p.m. ET from AT&T Stadium in Arlington. TOP PICK Cardinals vs Cowboys prediction: Cowboys -6.5 The Dallas Cowboys broke out of a two-game funk in which the offense stalled out on third downs. Against the Eagles, the Cowboys finished 9-for-14 on third/fourth downs and reclaimed their spot among the Top 5 attacks in Week 7. The Arizona Cardinals defense has been at the mercy of a very tough schedule, and it shows in its ratings (28th in EPA/play). While the offense was able to counter its opponents' scores earlier in the year, Arizona's attack is sputtering with the third-lowest points per play average over the last three contests. Dallas is more than happy turning this game into a track meet and thrives on the clean indoor surface at AT&T Stadium. Dak Prescott especially enjoys Jerry's World, with his career metrics spiking at home (103.4 rating at home vs. 92.8 on the road). This is Dallas' first "normal" home game since Week 2 (it played TNF at home in Week 5), and I'm grabbing this Cowboys offense short of the key number of a touchdown. Cardinals vs Cowboys combo Arizona was in a similar shootout spot with the Lions a few weeks back and couldn't keep pace with an explosive offense. Dallas does the same here, pulling away with plenty of points in the second half. CeeDee Lamb is coming off a two-TD day in Week 7 and faces a Cardinals defense allowing the second most touchdowns to rival receivers. Arizona WR Michael Wilson needs to be more involved, and Mike LaFleur knows it. With Arizona playing from behind, plenty of passes come his way, and projections call for as many as 70 yards on Sunday. Our Week 8 expert combo picks have more same-game parlay ideas across the slate. CeeDee Lamb anytime touchdown Michael Wilson 60+ receiving yards Cardinals vs Cowboys touchdown scorer: CeeDee Lamb Lamb looks like the best receiver in the NFL and is coming off a huge performance on Monday, catching two touchdown passes to give him six scores on the season. He will rip through an Arizona secondary ranked among the worst in the land but also featuring plenty of bodies on the injury report in Week 8. The Cardinals run one of the highest rates of zone coverage, and Lamb is excellent at spotting seams in that defense. He's not only a downfield threat but also a catch-and-run weapon, exploiting an Arizona stop unit giving up the seventh most yards after the catch. The Cardinals have allowed 10 touchdowns to WRs (second most), and Lamb's TD forecasts for Week 8 all sit at 60% or higher, with some projections at 80%. For more scorer ideas, see our Week 8 anytime touchdown picks . Cardinals vs Cowboys player prop: Michael Wilson 60+ receiving yards Arizona head coach Mike LaFleur was asked about Michael Wilson's surprising lack of involvement in recent weeks, even with former WR1 Marvin Harrison Jr. traded away. LaFleur danced around the probing question, telling the media, "At receiver, all you can do is control what you can control." Wilson's targets have tanked in the past three games, drawing 22 collective balls for four catches in each of those outings. He's put forth receiving efforts of 30, 32, and 55 yards. He had 13 and 17 targets in the two games prior to that power outage, reeling in 18 receptions for a total of 184 yards. Sunday's trip to Dallas is a pass-positive game script for the large road underdog and while QB Jacoby Brissett has fallen off a cliff, he faces a soft Cowboys secondary making all QBs look like Pro Bowlers (opponent passer rating of 105.2). Brissett is at his best against man coverage and faces a Dallas defense running a higher rate of man-on-man than most secondaries. Wilson rates out as the Cardinals' top one-on-one receiver. Most of his Week 8 projections sit north of 60 yards with a ceiling of 70 yards receiving. home.headline: Injury Report: Week 8 vs Cowboys
home.blurb: The Cardinals had been cautious with the rookie running back, but after three practices, the coaching staff felt Love was healthy enough to return. "Even though he's he's been out for two weeks, none of these guys by November 1st are truly at 100 (percent)," coach Mike LaFleur said. "But he's feeling as good as he can feel you know so yeah kind of go from there." Who will be blocking for him might be the bigger question. Center Hjalte Froholdt is questionable to play after being limited on Thursday with a knee injury. He did not practice on Friday. If unable to play, Hayden Conner could slide to center and the Cardinals would start a different player at right guard for the fourth time this season. Defensively, some reinforcements could be on the way. After missing the last three weeks, safety Dewey Wingard (knee) logged a full week of practice. He is questionable to play, as is cornerback Max Melton after he missed last weekend with a knee issue. Dallas ruled out wide receiver KaVontae Turpin (ribs) and linebacker Dee Winters (calf). Six players are questionable to play including defensive tackle Kenny Clark (back) and wide receiver George Pickens (shoulder/hamstring). Wide receiver Michael Wilson (ribs) wore the yellow non-contact pinny for a second consecutive day. He told the media on Wednesday it is out of caution. Wilson was one of eight players limited for practice. Center Hjalte Froholdt appeared on the injury report and was limited with a knee injury. His status this weekend will be important to monitor since backup center Hayden Conner is currently playing right guard. The Cowboys were back at practice on Thursday. They opened up the 21-day practice window for defensive tackle Jonathan Bullard. Safety Caleb Downs (ankle), wide receiver George Pickens (shoulder/hamstring), and defensive tackle Quinnen Williams (hamstring) were limited. Wide receiver Michael Wilson was wearing a yellow non-contact jersey. He appeared on the injury report with a ribs issue. He was limited. Multiple players returned to practice after being inactive on Sunday. Jeremiyah Love (ankle), safety Dewey Wingard (knee), cornerback Max Melton (knee), and quarterback Carson Beck (back) were limited. Cornerback Kei'Trel Clark was limited with an illness. Since the Cowboys did not practice on Wednesday, the designations were estimations. Wide receiver George Pickens was limited and listed with a shoulder and hamstring issue. I picked every dog against the spread last week and it looked good early, but then it collapsed late with five straight losses, including both prime-time games Sunday and Monday night. I was 8-6 straight up last week and 6-7-1 against the spread. Hey, the spread record was an improvement, which tells you how bad I've been this season. My ATS record this year is 43-61-3, which is a long way from .500. My straight-up record is 62-44-1. So this week, it's back to just picking the games. Forget all dogs. Trying to get to .500 makes me borrow a coaching cliché they all use. One game at a time. One week at a time. Turnaround time. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Lamar Jackson could be back for the Ravens, but how much will his injured ankle impact his ability to move? The Bills are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. Baltimore's defense was bad in the loss to the Bengals last week, but Buffalo's defense has been awful. Look for a shootout here with Josh Allen getting the best of it. Pick: Bills 35, Ravens 30 Tennessee Titans at Cincinnati Bengals (-10.5) The Titans are having major problems on offense, while the Bengals lit up the Ravens last week. Joe Burrow was special in the second half of that game and I think that will carry over here. Look for an offensive explosion from the Bengals as Burrow starts to get into the MVP talk. Pick: Bengals 36, Titans 10 Arizona Cardinals at Dallas Cowboys (-6.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Cowboys' offense came alive against the Eagles Monday night, especially on the ground, which isn't a good thing for an Arizona defense that is last in the league in scoring. The Dallas offense should roll and the Arizona offense won't be able to keep up. Dallas big — even on a short week. Pick: Cowboys 37, Cardinals 21 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) The undefeated Vikings face a tough road game here against Detroit. The Lions offense against the Minnesota defense will be a treat to watch. Jared Goff is playing at a high level right now, but Minnesota's defense is the best in the league in terms of scoring. The Vikings offense is limited, but the Detroit defense has had major problems. But they were better last week, which I think carries over. Lions take it. Pick: Lions 23, Vikings 13 Las Vegas Raiders at New York Jets (-1.5) Kirk Cousins stays in as the starter for the Raiders, but teams have blitzed him the past two weeks. The Vikings, which have yet to lose a game this season (6-0), are coming off a 16-10 win over the Indianapolis Colts. Meanwhile, Detroit defeated Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers a week ago, 20-17. Without further ado, here are the predictions from the Detroit Lions On SI staff for the Lions' Week 8 matchup with Minnesota. Christian Booher The Lions have a chance to truly solidify themselves as division title contenders with a win over the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday. Though the Vikings have underwhelmed offensively at times, they have found a way to start the season 6-0, thanks in part to a dominant defense that will be the best unit Detroit has faced to date. As a result, the pressure will be on Detroit's offense to come up with answers for a group that is led by one of the best defensive minds in football in Vikings coordinator Brian Flores. Jared Goff holds the key, as if he can get the ball out quickly and find answers within the opposition he will have a good chance to lead his group to a dominant performance. It's also an opportunity for the Lions' defense to make a statement against Kyler Murray. I think this game will feature turnovers on both sides, with the unit that gets the ball last ultimately finding a way to win. Detroit gets that advantage, as Goff leads Detroit to a game-winning field goal and a statement division victory. The Lions find a way to win ugly, and remind the league that they are capable of making a playoff run. Lions 23, Vikings 20 The Detroit Lions will face arguably their toughest test of the season yet when they square off with the undefeated Minnesota Vikings Sunday. The Vikings’ defense has been the definition of elite this season, allowing a measly 12.3 points per game (No. 1 in the NFL). You combine that with a stingy pass defense, and Lions signal-caller Jared Goff should have his hands full in the Week 8 affair. Plus, Detroit's defensive back and linebacker groups will need to bring their “A game” against Minnesota pass-catchers Justin Jefferson and T.J. Hockenson. It won't be easy for the Lions to emerge victorious in this divisional contest. However, I believe they will on the heels of strong efforts from their pass-rush and star running back Jahmyr Gibbs. I believe that Gibbs will help seal the deal for Detroit with several key runs in the fourth quarter, ultimately setting up Jake Bates for the game-winning kick. Lions 24, Vikings 21 John Maakaron This is a game the Lions would ideally like to get out to an early lead, as the Vikings offense is far behind the defense. Brian Flores is sure to bring the pressure from a variety of different spots, but Jared Goff should be able to make good decisions and distribute the football to Detroit’s skill position players. The most interesting matchup may end up being the Vikings offense against Detroit’s defense, given that both units are the clear weaknesses of their respective teams. Expect Jahmyr Gibbs to be responsible for another heavy workload at Ford Field. Lions 23, Vikings 17 Emmett Matasovsky The Lions take on the undefeated Minnesota Vikings in a headline matchup for Week 8. Overall, I see this being a slightly higher-scoring matchup than last week’s divisional showdown between the Packers and Lions. The Vikings defense is not exactly stout, ranking 23rd in the league in total defense. Combine that with Detroit having a series of unforced errors while breaking Cade Mays into game action at center, and it is hard to see the Lions not outscoring their 20 points last week. Kyler Murray is a mobile quarterback, and that has been a trend of a noticeable struggle for Detroit defenses. That said, the Vikings’ offensive greatness in their first six games also has come against the second-easiest schedule in the league. I see Detroit giving the Vikings the first mark in the latter’s loss column, with Jared Goff making several key plays. Kyler Murray Injury Update Causes Minor Shift to Vikings' Odds vs. Bills in NFL Week 9 Skip to main content ON SI Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray suffered a hamstring issue in Week 8 of the 2026 season, as the team lost to the Detroit Lions. According to Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell, Murray has a "sore" hamstring and will have a full evaluation before the team resumes practice this week. The Vikings don't play until Monday night against the Buffalo Bills in Week 9, so Murray will have an extra day to get healthy. If Murray is unable to go in Week 9, the Vikings would turn to veteran Carson Wentz at quarterback. Since Minnesota traded away former first-round pick J.J. McCarthy, Wentz and Max Brosmer are the only two remaining quarterbacks on the roster. DraftKings Sportbsook had moved the Vikings to 2.5-point underdogs at home in this matchup, but the line has since shifted back up to Minnesota +3.5. The Vikings opened as three-point underdogs on Sunday night , but they were gaining ground at home before the Murray update was released. Clearly, the betting market is bracing for the former No. 1 overall pick potentially missing Monday's matchup. This season, Murray has completed 64.9 percent of his passes for 1,022 yards, five scores and three picks while adding 29 carries for 167 yards on the ground. He was banged up early in the season with a concussion, leading to Wentz playing the majority of the team's first two games against Green Bay and Chicago. The Vikings' offense has not been good in the 2026 season, ranking 30th in the league in EPA/Play and 31st in success rate. However, elite play by the team's defense has kept it in first place in the NFC North at 6-1. For now, the betting market isn't reacting too much ahead of this marquee matchup on Monday night. away.headline: Jack Campbell update: Detroit Lions share positive news after scary neck injury against Vikings in NFL Week 8 clash
away.source: The Sunday Guardian Live on MSN
away.blurb: While the overnight hospital stay provides some clarity about the immediate plan, the Lions have not revealed a diagnosis, the extent of the injury or a possible recovery timeline. For now, Campbell will remain under medical observation, and the team says it will share further information when it becomes available. India, Nov. 2 -- The Detroit Lions have shared a fresh update on linebacker Jack Campbell after he suffered a worrying neck injury during their 19-15 win over the Minnesota Vikings in Week 8. Campbell was hurt while attempting to tackle Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson, prompting concern among players and fans as he received medical attention. The team has not yet confirmed the nature or severity of the injury, but its latest statement offered some reassurance. Campbell is currently resting at a local hospital and will stay overnight as doctors continue to evaluate and monitor his condition. Detroit Lions Provide Positive Update on Jack Campbell After Frightening Neck Injury The Detroit Lions confirmed Sunday evening that Jack Campbell will remain at a local hospital overnight after suffering a neck injury against the Minnesota Vikings. In their latest statement, the team said: "Jack Campbell is resting and will remain in a local hospital tonight, for continued evaluation and monitoring. The team will provide further updates as we have them." The update came hours after the linebacker was hurt while tackling Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson on the opening play of the fourth quarter. Campbell remained on the field for several minutes as medical staff attended to him before he was placed on a backboard and taken away on a cart. The incident left players on both teams visibly shaken, with several Lions teammates gathering around their captain. He was subsequently transported to a nearby hospital for further assessment. Head coach Dan Campbell offered a brief update after the game, confirming that the linebacker was breathing and alert when he left the stadium. "He's breathing, he's alert when he left. I know nothing further. Thoughts and prayers are with Jack. I would ask that everyone does the same," the coach said, as the team waited for more information from medical personnel. Lions' Win Overshadowed by Campbell's Injury as Team Awaits Further Medical Updates The injury cast a shadow over Detroit's 19-15 victory, which improved its record to 5-2 and handed Minnesota its first defeat of the season. The result would ordinarily have been a significant moment for the Lions, but concern for Campbell quickly became the focus. Quarterback Jared Goff also shared an emotional message about his teammate, highlighting the importance of remembering Campbell and his family during the difficult moment.

away.headline: Vikings-Lions Final Injury Report
away.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being 'uncertain' of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Lions, Kerby Joseph had his three-week window opened to return from IR this week but will not return this week. Starting slot cornerback Roger McCreary was a late addition to the Lions' injury report on Friday, when he was limited with a foot injury. He is questionable for Sunday's game, which means he's likely to play. For the Vikings, close to a clean sheet with just a late addition of Jay Ward to the injury report on Friday with knee issue. home.headline: Detroit Lions signing veteran LB off Patriots practice squad
home.blurb: According to a report from ESPN’s Adam Schefter, the Detroit Lions are signing veteran linebacker K.J. Britt off of the New England Patriots’ practice squad. The move comes after Detroit suffered two linebacker injuries on Sunday against the Minnesota Vikings. Rookie Jimmy Rolder suffered a season-ending hamstring injury , while Jack Campbell remains in the hospital with a neck injury . No specifics are known at this point about Campbell’s situation, but the team did say that early developments were “positive.” Britt was a fifth-round draft pick for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2021, and ended up playing 59 games for them over four seasons—including 15 starts. Last year, he was with the Miami Dolphins, playing in all 17 games and starting one. This year, he failed to make the Patriots’ 53-man roster, but they kept him around on the practice squad, and he was elevated for the team’s Week 5 game against the Raiders. For most of his career, Britt has served as a special teamer. Across just over five seasons in the NFL, Britt has played 1,303 special teams snaps vs. 994 on defense—and he has logged over 250 special teams snaps in four of his first five NFL seasons. There’s a good chance that will be Britt’s role early in Detroit. With the Lions likely to lean more heavily on the likes of Malcolm Rodriguez, Derrick Barnes, and Trevor Nowaske on defense—with potentially Amen Ogbongbemiga and Joe Bachie mixed in—the Lions will need more experienced depth on special teams and reserves on defense. Britt should be a relatively good fit in Detroit, as a high-effort player who was a captain at Auburn. Detroit should have a good handle on who Britt is as a person and player, as he overlapped with current Lions defensive line coach Kacy Rodgers during his entire time with the Buccaneers.
