Kickoff is set for 1 p.m. ET from MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, N.J. The game will broadcast live on FOX. The Jets are 1.5-point favorites on the spread (Jets -1.5; -112), with the over/under set at 46.5. New York is a -125 moneyline favorite while Las Vegas is a +105 underdog. Let's get into my Raiders vs Jets prediction for today's AFC clash. Raiders vs Jets pick: Jets -1.5 (-110) My Raiders vs. Jets best bet is New York to cover the spread (-1.5), with the best price currently available at FanDuel. Make sure to find the best odds by checking our live NFL odds page. Raiders vs Jets Odds Raiders vs Jets Spread : Raiders +1.5 (-108), Jets -1.5 (-112) Raiders vs Jets Moneyline : Raiders +105, Jets -125 Raiders vs Jets Total : 46.5 Raiders vs Jets Preview Raiders Preview This is purely a situational fade of a Raiders team that has "letdown" written all over them. Las Vegas is traveling all the way across the country for an early kick in potential bad weather after an absolutely grueling four-game stretch against the Rams , Bills , Patriots , and Chiefs . The Raiders are bruised, battered, and emotionally drained. The Raiders defense looked great in Weeks 1-2 against Miami and Los Angeles (Chargers), but that was a complete mirage. Since Week 3, the Raiders are basically the worst defense in the NFL across every single major metric. The Raiders also cannot run the football on offense, ranking dead last in both Rush EPA and Rush Success Rate despite investing a first-round draft pick in Ashton Jeanty last year. Without a mobile quarterback to bail them out, this offense is entirely one-dimensional. The Jets are 1-4 in one-possession games and have been a bit unlucky, but the main factor here is that their offense should finally be fully healthy. The Jets have dealt with injuries from the jump, but things are looking up on that front. Getting Dylan Parham back is a huge upgrade at guard, Breece Hall and Braelon Allen are good to go in the backfield, Adonai Mitchell is back to stretch the defense, rookie Omar Cooper looks great, and both tight ends Kenyon Sadiq and Mason Taylor are healthy. Geno Smith should finally have a full arsenal to work with in this game, or something close to it. Smith throws short on roughly 55% of his passes, which bodes well in a matchup against a Raiders defense that is the worst in the league against short passing attacks. Yes, the Jets' run defense is problematic (24th in Rush EPA, 25th in Success Rate), and they are dealing with injuries to the defensive line, but as I mentioned above, Las Vegas doesn't have the rushing attack to take advantage of it. Raiders vs Jets Spread Pick to Make This is a terrible travel spot for a bad Raiders team coming off a brutal scheduling gauntlet. The Jets have clear schematic advantages through the air, and their defensive weakness against the run probably won't be exposed by this Las Vegas's running backs. I'll back New York to cover the short number here. Neither team is looking too hot at the moment. The Raiders are on a four-game losing streak and the Jets just lost to the previously winless Dolphins . To get a feel for how this one could play out, we get the takes from the Raiders Wire staff. Game picks for Raiders Week 8 matchup vs Jets Lance Fernandez -- Jets 24, Raiders 20 The Jets have struggled offensively, ranking in the bottom half in passing yards, rushing yards, and points per game. However, playing against a defense that has surrendered the fourth-most points per game and playing at home should give New York's offense a boost. That and the Jets' solid pass defense should keep the Raiders' losing streak going. Marvin Uzor -- Raiders 24, Jets 20 The Jets have been the NFL's slowest-starting offense since last season, so this is the week the Raiders finally don't have to dig out of an early hole. Put Kirk Cousins against a defense with one interception in 24 games, and I think the losing streak ends at four. Lamarr Fields -- Raiders 24. Jets 17 The Raiders will have some success running the ball and getting pressure on Geno Smith. Look for Brock Bowers and Tre Tucker to have good games. Levi Damien -- Raiders 20, Jets 19 Nothing about this Raiders team right now inspires confidence in me. And it isn't because they've lost four straight. It's the manner in which they lost them. Either just getting flat out streamrolled or giving up a ton of points and then trying to make a comeback when it's too late. The offensive line is starting to look like who we thought they were and the defense simply doesn't look smart. And playing on the east coast? Ugh. That being said, I have less confidence in Geno Smith. Perhaps that comes from the experience with him in Las Vegas last season, who knows. But I think the Jets record reflects that he's not the answer, with their only wins coming over a hapless Titans team and a low-scoring affair against the Browns. And they're coming off handing the Dolphins their first win of the season. The same Dolphins team the Raiders put a hurting on in the opener. I see a close one here. away.headline: Darien Porter Injury: Why Did Raiders CB Leave Jets Game on Opening Play?
away.blurb: Las Vegas Raiders cornerback Darien Porter is questionable to return with a groin injury after going down without contact on the opening snap in the game against the New York Jets Sunday. Rookie Jermod McCoy took over for him at outside corner . The team then listed Porter as questionable with a groin injury . Raiders Should Trade for Rumored Patriots DT Available for Low-Cost Before Deadline Darien Porter Injury: Why Did Raiders CB Leave Jets Game on Opening Play? Unlock the latest Heavy on Raiders news — direct to your inbox. The injury came at MetLife Stadium against the Jets in Week 8, and it leaves the Raiders watching the sideline to see whether a key cornerback can come back. Jets quarterback Geno Smith hit wide receiver Garrett Wilson on a long completion to start the game, with accounts of the gain ranging from 31 to 41 yards. Porter hit the turf without being touched , according to the Las Vegas Review-Journal . Trainers helped Porter to the medical tent on the Raiders' sideline with the score still 0-0. He later emerged and was trying to regain his mobility under trainers' watchful eyes, according to Raiders beat writer Sam Warren. Why Isn’t Fernando Mendoza Playing for the Raiders Today? Insider Gives Timeline Las Vegas Raiders' Darien Porter Career Background Porter, 25, was born Jan. 6, 2001, in Bettendorf, Iowa, and is listed at 6 feet 2 inches and 195 pounds . He played receiver and cornerback at Bettendorf High School, catching 27 passes for 440 yards and seven touchdowns as a senior, and won a Class 4A state title in the 400 meters. He spent time at Iowa State from 2019 through 2024 , starting at receiver before moving to defensive back. Special teams made up most of his early role. He became a full-time starter in 2024, finishing with 18 tackles, two tackles for loss, three interceptions and two passes defended, and earned honorable mention All-Big 12 recognition. Porter ran an unofficial 4.30-second 40-yard dash at the NFL Scouting Combine. The Raiders selected Porter in the third round of the 2025 draft, 68th overall. As a rookie, he played all 17 games, starting 10 , and totaled 42 tackles, three passes defended and one fumble recovery. His rookie contract runs through 2028 . This season, Porter missed Week 2 against the Chargers because of a foot injury against the Dolphins in the opener. That was a separate issue from Sunday's injury. Before it, he had been targeted five times in that opener and allowed one catch for 12 yards , according to Pro Football Focus . Raiders Announce Ashton Jeanty Decision 90 Minutes Before Patriots Game How the Las Vegas Raiders Adjust Without Darien Porter The Raiders have options at outside corner. McCoy, selected in the fourth round of 2026 , slid in the draft after a previous knee injury and stepped into the lineup immediately. Rookie Jermod McCoy took over for him at outside corner . The team then listed Porter as questionable with a groin injury . Unlock the latest Heavy on Raiders news — direct to your inbox. The injury came at MetLife Stadium against the Jets in Week 8, and it leaves the Raiders watching the sideline to see whether a key cornerback can come back. Jets quarterback Geno Smith hit wide receiver Garrett Wilson on a long completion to start the game, with accounts of the gain ranging from 31 to 41 yards. Porter hit the turf without being touched , according to the Las Vegas Review-Journal . Trainers helped Porter to the medical tent on the Raiders' sideline with the score still 0-0. He later emerged and was trying to regain his mobility under trainers' watchful eyes, according to Raiders beat writer Sam Warren. Why Isn’t Fernando Mendoza Playing for the Raiders Today? Insider Gives Timeline Las Vegas Raiders' Darien Porter Career Background Porter, 25, was born Jan. 6, 2001, in Bettendorf, Iowa, and is listed at 6 feet 2 inches and 195 pounds . He played receiver and cornerback at Bettendorf High School, catching 27 passes for 440 yards and seven touchdowns as a senior, and won a Class 4A state title in the 400 meters. He spent time at Iowa State from 2019 through 2024 , starting at receiver before moving to defensive back. Special teams made up most of his early role. He became a full-time starter in 2024, finishing with 18 tackles, two tackles for loss, three interceptions and two passes defended, and earned honorable mention All-Big 12 recognition. Porter ran an unofficial 4.30-second 40-yard dash at the NFL Scouting Combine. The Raiders selected Porter in the third round of the 2025 draft, 68th overall. As a rookie, he played all 17 games, starting 10 , and totaled 42 tackles, three passes defended and one fumble recovery. His rookie contract runs through 2028 . This season, Porter missed Week 2 against the Chargers because of a foot injury against the Dolphins in the opener. That was a separate issue from Sunday's injury. Before it, he had been targeted five times in that opener and allowed one catch for 12 yards , according to Pro Football Focus . The Browns are no easy challenge this time around, and the Steelers learned that firsthand several weeks ago. The Browns won their first meeting on Thursday Night Football, but the matchup shifts to Acrisure Stadium for Week 8, and the Steelers intend to exact some revenge on their divisional foes. Both squads enter with a 5-2 record and a share of the AFC North lead. It’s a measuring-stick showdown between the Steelers and Browns, and bold actions will be taken. Both Teams Score 25 Points or More Both of these franchises bring strong defenses to their Week 8 contest. The Steelers rank in the top 10 in total yards allowed per game, rushing yards allowed per game and points allowed per contest. They also rank 11th in passing yards allowed per game. Similarly, the Browns rank in the top 15 across multiple defensive categories. It’s going to be a matchup of two stout defensive units, right? Well what would be more surprising than these two teams putting up an offensive showdown? That’s what could be in store for these two teams, despite all signs pointing toward the opposite. The Steelers rank 22nd in the NFL in points per game, posting an average of 21.9. The Browns trail, recording the 28th-best average of 19.0 points per game. But, the Steelers have also reached the 24-point mark four times in seven tries, and they could put up even more in Week 8. Oct 11, 2026; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Germie Bernard (17) carries the ball in the second half against the Indianapolis Colts at Acrisure Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Aaron Rodgers Hits 300 Yards for First Time With Steelers Aaron Rodgers Hits 300 Yards for First Time With Steelers If the Steelers are going to buck the trend and put up points, there are two approaches to help accomplish that. One is to exploit their 19th-ranked run defense, which has to be at the top of their game plan as Jaylen Warren continues to put up MVP-caliber production. Another avenue, the more unexpected one for the offense to take, is to push the ball downfield with the passing game. In the team’s first matchup against the Browns, Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf posted five receptions on nine targets for 115 yards. And they managed to break off his biggest play of the game by getting him away from Cleveland’s top defender, Denzel Ward. If the Steelers can capture that again in Week 8, quarterback Aaron Rodgers could have a magical day. In 2025, Rodgers never hit the 300-yard mark. His 2026 season high so far is 299 yards, which he threw for during that previous contest against the Browns. In the three weeks since, he hasn’t surpassed 255 yards, but this could be the one where he eclipses 300 yards. Germie 100-Yard Game Incoming If Rodgers is throwing that many yards, one of his receivers has to have an outstanding day on the stat sheet. After he earned more and more trust, Bernard could face a favorable matchup if he doesn’t go against Ward too often. He’s gotten close, putting up two 80+ yard games so far this season. This week, it finally happens. The second-round pick eclipses 100 yards for the first time in his young NFL career. picks.blurb: Steelers vs. Browns: 4 bold predictions for this week's game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football NFL Power Rankings Week 9 Waiver Wire Bears beat Seahawks MLB award finalists NBA Power Rankings Steelers vs. Browns: 4 bold predictions for this week's game Curt Popejoy, Steelers Wire Sat, October 31, 2026 at 6:36 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads This week, the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cleveland Browns square off, both teams at 5-2 and tied on top in the AFC North. The Steelers are looking for payback and the Browns are looking for their first sweep of the Steelers since 1988. Here are four bold predictions for this week's game. Jaylen Warren carries the offense The Browns run defense is struggling and Jaylen Warren is on a tear. Warren rushed for 93 yards in the first matchup and our bold prediction for Warren this week is he gets his fourth 100-yard rushing game of the year and tops 150 yards of total offense and two total touchdowns. T.J. Watt breaks out with 3 sacks This week is the perfect opportunity for T.J. Watt to quiet the critics as he faces backup right tackle Dawand Jones. Watt is currently fourth int he NFL with 5.5 sacks but has struggled with consistent pressure. This week he breaks out of his funk with a huge three-sack performance and one of them turns into a huge forced fumble. Pittsburgh solves their red zone woes with two scores For all the things he can do, head coach Mike McCarthy has struggled to get the Steelers red-zone offense on track. This is due in large part because he's been unwilling to just run the football near the goal line. That ends this week with two short rushing touchdowns. The Steelers currently have only one rushing touchdown all season. Double-digit win for the Steelers We appreciate what the Browns are building but Pittsburgh is at home and riding a three-game win streak since the loss to Cleveland and will keep it going with a double-digit win, bringing the Browns back to Earth about their place in the AFC North. Final score prediction: Steelers 35, Browns 24 This article originally appeared on Steelers Wire: Steelers vs. Browns: 4 bold predictions for this week's game

picks.blurb: Steelers vs. Browns: Week 8 game picks - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football NFL Power Rankings Week 9 Waiver Wire Bears beat Seahawks MLB award finalists NBA Power Rankings Steelers vs. Browns: Week 8 game picks (Photo by Frank Jansky/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Jarrett Bailey Sat, October 31, 2026 at 3:19 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads First place in the AFC North is up for grabs as the Pittsburgh Steelers host the Cleveland Browns. Both teams enter the day at 5-2, with Cleveland holding a 1-0 head-to-head advantage over Pittsburgh. Will they beat the Steelers on the road in a regular season game for the first time since 2003? Our staff weighs in. Mike Nicastro : The Steelers haven't lost to the Browns twice in a season in almost three decades, but this year presents a unique challenge. Teams traveling internationally over the last two seasons are just 1-7 when returning to face a team that did not travel overseas the prior week. That one win was the Broncos last season, when they scored 33 4th quarter points against the Giants to win by 1 point. Fatigue will play a factor, but having home field will help significantly. This is still a Browns team that lost to the Jets on the road, and just went to the wire with the Titans. Won't be surprised if its ugly, but Pittsburgh rides the run game again into their bye. Steelers 20 Browns 17. Jason Aponte: This will be a dogfight between the division rivals. The Steelers have shown improvement offensively lately and will need to beat Cleveland's plan of man coverage. Rodgers and the offense does enough and the defense holds up to give Pittsburgh the division lead. Steelers 21, Browns 17. Ryan Parish : The Steelers were the better team in 3 out of 4 quarters the last time these teams met a few weeks ago. Both teams have found a groove since, and they enter the contest at 5-2. Winner leaves the game atop the AFC North. I've had a running bit in these predictions that will not change until it stops working. Browns 24-Steelers 23. Austin Bechtold: The Steelers haven't lost to the Browns at home in the regular season since I was two. I can't fathom it happening with how the Steelers defense is playing right now. I've been wrong about Patrick Graham and doubted his scheme to a degree early in the season, but if he calls a great gameplan Sunday I'm sold. Aaron Rodgers is playing his best football since 2021. The Browns aren't the old Browns and I think are better than people are giving credit for. The Steelers do what it takes, and will be in sole possession of first place in the AFC North on Sunday. Steelers 24-18. Ryland Bickley : This is a series that has been defined by home teams winning as of late, and with the Steelers on a hot streak and playing in Acrisure this Sunday, I don't expect that to change. Cleveland's man coverage scheme should once again prove a challenge for the Pittsburgh offense, but the Steelers defense has taken some strides since the last matchup. Steelers 27, Browns 20 . Joey Bray : When these teams take the field on Sunday, the Pittsburgh Steelers will be exactly one month removed from suffering another loss to the Browns in Cleveland on Thursday Night Football. Since that game, the Steelers have won three straight. I can't say for certain how much the team has grown since then, as they still have concerns in the secondary on defense and struggles in the red zone as an offense. Unlike last time where the browns jumped out to a big lead early, I think this game will be a close one throughout. The Browns are a much better football team that anyone anticipated entering the season. Todd Monken deserves a ton of credit for the way he has continued to put Deshaun Watson and the offense in positions to win. However, all five of their wins have come on game winning drives, a trend that is unlikely to continue. I'll take Pittsburgh to get their revenge on Cleveland and go into the bye week with sole possession of first place in the AFC North. Steelers 21, Browns 20 . Jarrett Bailey: I said ahead of the Saints game that I don't know if the Steelers are a team I'd bank on winning four games in a row, yet here we are after a three-game win streak. The whole "Cleveland hasn't won in Pittsburgh since 2003" doesn't necessarily mean much to me in terms of results. Although it does seem to matter when these two teams play in Cleveland that the Steelers turn into the worst versions of themselves. I do think the Steelers win, but I'm not going to take this Browns team lightly. Steelers 20, Browns 16. Let us know what you think in the comments . picks.blurb: Steelers vs. Browns Prediction: Why Pittsburgh Gets Revenge for Week 4 Loss at Home - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football NFL Power Rankings Week 9 Waiver Wire Bears beat Seahawks MLB award finalists NBA Power Rankings Jobe Morrison Sun, November 1, 2026 at 5:00 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Pittsburgh Steelers get their shot at revenge Sunday when the Cleveland Browns come to town for a Week 8 AFC North rematch . Cleveland beat Pittsburgh in Week 4 by taking advantage of a soft zone defense and an offense that had not yet found its footing. A lot has changed since then. The Steelers' offense has settled in, the defense has mixed up its looks, and Pittsburgh has a clear edge on the ground against a Browns defense that has struggled to stop the run. Here is why the Steelers will even the season series at home. Prediction: Steelers Win 23-16 Pittsburgh Steelers running back Jaylen Warren (30) runs after catch against the Cleveland Browns during the third quarter at Acrisure Stadium.Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images When the Steelers played the Browns in Week 4, the offense was coming off its first big performance of the season, against the Bengals in Week 3. It still hadn't found its groove. Seven games in, the offense looks much better than it did early in the season, and three games after the loss to Cleveland, it's no longer fair to say it hasn't found its rhythm. Pittsburgh also has an advantage in the run game against this Browns defense . Cleveland has struggled to stop the run consistently, and it allowed three rushing touchdowns and more than 100 rushing yards to the Titans last week. The only concern for Pittsburgh is the passing game. It has produced for most of the season, but it hasn't been as consistent as the Steelers want. Can it take a step forward in this divisional grudge match at home? Sep 18, 2023; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson (4) is sacked by Pittsburgh Steelers safety Elijah Riley (37) during the fourth quarter at Acrisure Stadium. Pittsburgh won 26-22. Credit: Charles LeClaire-USA TODAY Sports Let's be honest: The Steelers should have held the Browns to far fewer points in Week 4. To Cleveland's credit, it took advantage of the Steelers' soft zone plan, missed tackles and miscommunications. Since then, the Steelers have mixed up their looks and have graded out as a strong defense by the analytics. There's no excuse for them not to play at a high level at home Sunday. It will be up to the defense to play tighter coverage, make sound tackles and pressure the quarterback. The Steelers have done all three well this season. If they do them again Sunday, they will have a good chance to win. home.headline: Steelers reportedly linked to star WR ahead of NFL trade deadline
home.blurb: The biggest issue for the Steelers’ receiver room, though, is injuries. Three receivers sit on the injured reserve list: Michael Pittman Jr., Roman Wilson and Cole Burgess. Ben Skowronek is also out with a calf strain right now. That leaves Metcalf and standout rookie Germie Bernard as the top receivers on the team right now. The Steelers have also utilized top running back Jaylen Warren as a receiver this season as he has posted the second most receiving yards (294). The Pittsburgh Steelers might be interested in acquiring a wide receiver in a trade ahead of the NFL deadline on Tuesday, Nov. 10. The team’s top receiver, DK Metcalf, isn’t producing like they’d hoped so far this season. Through eight games, Metcalf has caught 33 of 65 passes thrown to him for 378 yards and one touchdown. Understandably, the Steelers are now reportedly interested in getting a new wide receiver for quarterback Aaron Rodgers , and one name that’s popped up this week is New York Jets star Garrett Wilson, NFL insider Jason La Canfora floated the idea on Monday . Last week, Wilson told reporters that he doesn’t want to request a trade from the Jets, but that he’s aware of how the NFL’s business runs. He will definitely be an expensive get for whichever team decides to make an offer. Wilson, who was the 2022 NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year, is in his fifth season in New York. He’s shined with the Jets, but the team has still failed to make the playoffs dating back to the 2010 season. He might want to join a team that has postseason potential. And, he would likely be a long-term solution for the Steelers’ offensive goals. The receiver has experience playing with Rodgers when he was on the Jets in 2024 (he played one snap in ’23). Wilson put up his best stats with Rodgers in ’24 as he caught 101 passes for 1,104 yards and seven touchdowns that season. Maybe the partnership needs to reunite in Pittsburgh. picks.blurb: FalconsSI Staff Split on Falcons vs. Buccaneers Week 8 Predictions Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Atlanta Falcons have an opportunity to make a major statement in Week 8 when they travel to face the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday. Coming off an impressive victory over the previously undefeated San Francisco 49ers, Atlanta has a chance to carry that momentum into a divisional matchup with significant NFC South implications. The Buccaneers are coming off a blowout victory over the Carolina Panthers, but their 2-5 record leaves them needing a win to keep their divisional hopes alive. Meanwhile, a Falcons victory would give Atlanta sole possession of first place in the NFC South. Here is how the FalconsSI staff sees Sunday’s matchup playing out. Scott Kennedy (3-4) This is the ultimate Lucy and Charlie Brown game for Falcons fans. Atlanta is coming off an impressive home victory against the San Francisco 49ers, while Tampa Bay remains just 2-5 despite a blowout win over Carolina. The opportunity is there for the Falcons to take sole possession of first place in the NFC South and potentially put the Buccaneers’ divisional hopes on life support. This is exactly the kind of game Atlanta should win. Unfortunately, it is also the type of game the Falcons have dropped year after frustrating year. However, looking beyond the history of disappointment, Atlanta is playing better football than Tampa Bay right now. The Falcons and Buccaneers can both run and stop the run, but Atlanta is getting better quarterback play and has a better set of (healthy) weapons on offense. Bucky Irvin is a great back, but Bijan Robinson is an elite player. The rainy weather might keep the score down in this one, and it could help negate the Falcon's advantage through the air. Surely, Lucy keeps the football in place for Charlie Brown this time. Prediction: Falcons 23, Buccaneers 16 Gerald Thomas, III (3-4) Falcons-Buccaneers matchups always deliver compelling storylines, and Sunday’s meeting is no exception. There is Kevin Stefanski facing Baker Mayfield, Michael Penix Jr. making his long-awaited return to Tampa and Zac Robinson now serving as Atlanta’s offensive coordinator. Both teams enter the matchup following statement victories. Atlanta knocked off the previously undefeated 49ers, while Tampa Bay dominated the Panthers. A win would give the Falcons an opportunity to take over the top spot in the NFC South and continue building on their recent success. Prediction: Falcons 27, Buccaneers 17 Jerry Jones, Falcons Podcast (3-4) 99% of Falcons fans have deep-seated trauma, and games like this are exactly why. The Falcons are fresh off a win against arguably the best team in football and are facing a team that’s struggling. These are exactly the games the Falcons have inexplicably lost in recent years. That said, this is not a one-sided matchup. The Buccaneers are much better than their record suggests. They have a really good defense and have been excellent in the trenches on both sides of the ball. On top of that, all of the Buccaneers’ losses have been one-score games against teams above .500. I think this game will come down to how the Falcons’ o-line fares against the Bucs’ d-line. Michael Penix Jr. is an above-average quarterback when he’s playing ahead of the sticks and has a clean pocket. The other question is whether this o-line can create running lanes against one of the best run-defending d-lines in the league. I’m much more confident in how the Falcons’ defense stacks up against the Bucs’ offense. The defensive line has been playing great, and the Bucs’ banged-up receiving corps is overmatched against the Falcons' secondary. Ultimately, I have the Falcons winning this, but I think it will be a closer matchup than most expect. Prediction: Falcons 23, Buccaneers 20 Darius Hayes (3-4) I expect a tough, physical divisional battle with the weather playing a major factor in Sunday’s outcome. The Falcons should lean heavily on their running game to control the clock, establish the pace and keep Tampa Bay’s offense off the field. Atlanta cannot afford to get away from what worked against San Francisco. Establishing the run will help take pressure off Penix while creating opportunities for the offense to control the game. Defensively, the Falcons need to make enough key stops and force the Buccaneers into difficult situations. Tampa Bay is capable of making plays offensively, but Atlanta has shown improvements on that side of the ball. Coming off last week’s momentum-building victory over the 49ers, I like the Falcons to carry that confidence into Tampa. It won’t be easy, but Atlanta does enough on both sides of the ball to earn a hard-fought divisional victory, take over first place in the NFC South, and leave Tampa Bay with a win. Prediction: Falcons 24, Buccaneers 17 Garrett Chapman (3-4) The Falcons are fresh off their biggest win of the season, but they have to take the show on the road on Sunday. They've had a lot of success in Tampa over the last few years, and this team will enter with a lot of confidence with how Michael Penix has been playing. This will be a tight game that I expect will come down to the final drive. picks.blurb: Who the Experts Are Taking in Buccaneers vs. Falcons Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football NFL Power Rankings Week 9 Waiver Wire Bears beat Seahawks MLB award finalists NBA Power Rankings Who the Experts Are Taking in Buccaneers vs. Falcons Week 8 Sahil Goswami Sun, November 1, 2026 at 5:22 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The NFC South rivalry takes center stage on Sunday as the Atlanta Falcons visit the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium. Both teams enter the matchup with something to prove after recording impressive wins in Week 7. Conversely, the Falcons enter at 3-4, compared with Tampa Bay's 2-5 record. Atlanta will look to build on its defensive performance against the 49ers, while the Buccaneers hope to carry their improved rushing attack into another divisional contest. For this Week 8 NFC Showdown, the Buccaneers remain slight 2.5-point favorites, as per Sports Illustrated. Tampa Bay's moneyline is around -135, while Atlanta sits at +114. The game total is approximately 44.5 points. The Falcons have already beaten the previously undefeated 49ers and are 2-1 on the road. Michael Penix Jr. has shown improved command of the offense, while Bijan Robinson remains a major threat. National Predictions NFL.com: Buccaneers 27, Falcons 23 ESPN: Buccaneers 24, Falcons 20 CBS Sports: Buccaneers 23, Falcons 17 The Arizona Republic: Buccaneers 27, Falcons 20 Sports Illustrated: Falcons 23, Buccaneers 20 What Experts Are Saying "This NFC South bout features two dynamic rushing attacks and a pair of top-five run defenses. Atlanta's Bijan Robinson is the cream of this year's running back crop, leading the pack in rush yards (704) and scrimmage yards (907), while Tampa's Bucky Irving has gained 189 yards after forcing missed tackles this season, fifth-most league-wide. These two ball-carriers will make their plays, but this contest will be decided by which quarterback — Michael Penix Jr. or Baker Mayfield — can protect the ball and best execute through the air against defenses that hold notable advantages in NFL Pro's overall passing efficiency. Penix has played well in Kevin Stefanski's offense, throwing three TDs without an INT in consecutive games. Mayfield wasn't stressed much in last week's blowout win (he threw the ball 11 times), but he'll likely need to rely on that glove-wearing right hand to move the chains at times, if not make game-winning-type throws late. Getting Emeka Egbuka back would certainly help, and the status of RT Luke Goedeke (calf) looms large. I expect this to be a back-and-forth battle with both teams coming off statement wins, and I'm leaning the Bucs' way if this game does come down to the final minutes, as the Falcons are 0-3 in one-possession contests in 2026," Brooke Cersosimo, NFL.com "Stefanski is 6-17 against the spread and 5-18 outright as an underdog following a win. Bijan Robinson can't fix everything against Tampa Bay's run defense. So that puts more on Penix, whose past two games look better because of six touchdown passes. Tampa Bay has 10 sacks over its past two games. I expect more stalled drives than another touchdown spree," Pamela Maldonado, ESPN. "This is suddenly a big game in the NFC South with the Bucs upsetting Carolina last week and the Falcons upsetting the 49ers. The Tampa Bay running game has come alive, but Atlanta is stingy on the ground, giving up 3.8 per rush. That will mean this is a Baker Mayfield game. Tampa Bay gives up 3.5 per rush, which might make for tough going for Bijan Robinson. That's a problem for the Atlanta offense. Tampa Bay wins it," Pete Prisco, CBS Sports. "The Buccaneers' defense really impressed against the Panthers in Week 7. At 2-5, Tampa Bay is right in the thick of the NFC South race. Bucky Irving will keep them there with another solid performance against Atlanta," Jeremy Cluff, Arizona Republic. "The Falcons are the most mysterious team in the NFL. As they showed in Week 7 by handing the San Francisco 49ers their first loss of the season, the Falcons can beat any team in any given week, but they can also lose to any team. I think the Buccaneers are better than they showed early in the season. Their defense is third in opponent EPA per play, behind only the Vikings and Seahawks. They can also run the ball effectively, ranking inside the top 10 in both rush EPA and rush success rate. That means if Baker Mayfield can start to get into peak form, Tampa Bay will all of a sudden be a dangerous team to face. Tampa Bay may surprise some people in the coming weeks," Ryan Gilbert, Sports Illustrated. away.blurb: Head coach Kevin Stefanski announced Monday that defensive end Samson Ebukam and rookie wide receiver Zachariah Branch are dealing with hamstring injuries that will keep both players out of the Week 9 matchup. “Samson Ebukam, Zachariah Branch have hamstring injuries,” Stefanski said to open his Monday press conference. “That’s going to keep them out of this game. Not sure, long term, how many games those types of injuries will be, but we’ll obviously treat those and then see how it goes over the next couple of weeks.” Branch’s absence will also be felt, particularly in Atlanta’s return game. The Falcons selected the former USC wide receiver in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft to add another explosive element to their receiving corps while providing versatility as a return specialist. Branch exited Sunday’s loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers early after returning a kickoff and did not return to the game. The hamstring injury will now sideline him against Cincinnati. Losing Branch takes away an option who has provided Atlanta with opportunities to generate field position through the return game. Stefanski did not provide a definitive timetable for either player’s return, leaving open the possibility that their absences could extend beyond Sunday’s international game. Kendal Daniels Wasn't Only Falcons Rookie with a Dramatic Return vs. 49ers The Atlanta Falcons will be without two important players when they travel to Madrid, Spain, to face the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday. The injuries leave Atlanta without contributors on both sides of the football as the team begins preparations for its international matchup against Cincinnati. Ebukam’s Absence Impacts Defensive Line Rotation Ebukam has been a consistent presence in Atlanta’s defensive line rotation throughout his first season with the organization. The veteran defensive end joined the Falcons this offseason after spending the previous two seasons with the Indianapolis Colts. His arrival also reunited him with defensive line coach Nate Ollie, whom he previously worked with in Indianapolis. Through the first eight weeks of the season, Ebukam has recorded 2.5 sacks and 15 quarterback pressures, according to Next Gen Stats. His pressure total ranks fifth among Falcons defenders. His absence creates another challenge for Atlanta’s pass rush, which will need additional production from the remaining defensive line rotation against a Cincinnati offense led by quarterback Joe Burrow. The Falcons will likely need other defensive ends to take on expanded responsibilities while Ebukam recovers. Branch’s Injury Creates Another Challenge for Special Teams Although Branch has primarily served as a complementary option in the passing game, recording 10 receptions for 64 yards, his contributions on special teams have been more substantial. away.headline: NFL reinstates James Pearce Jr. after eight-game suspension: Why EDGE returns at critical time for Falcons
away.blurb: Pearce entered a 12-month pre-trial program, and once it is complete, all the charges will be dismissed. He must also stay out of legal trouble for a six-month period and attend therapy sessions as part of the agreement he and his representation reached in the case. During the legal proceedings, Pearce remained in communication with the Falcons and remained in good enough football shape to potentially be available for Week 9. Pearce's return could impact NFC South race Pearce is just one player who will be available for only about half of the season, but his return alone could uplift the Falcons in their hunt for the NFC South title. No team in the division owns more than three wins, and this race is trending toward delivering a sub-.500 champion for the second time in as many years. Since every game matters immensely in such a tight battle, one or two standout performances from Pearce could be the difference between spots in the standings. The NFL reinstated Atlanta Falcons edge rusher James Pearce Jr. on Monday, ending the eight-game suspension it handed down before the season began. Pearce will be eligible to play in Sunday's game against the Cincinnati Bengals in Madrid, and coach Kevin Stefanski said last week that the plan is for him to see action in the Week 9 contest. Stefanski said upon Pearce's reinstatement, though, that it is too early to tell how much he will play in his first game back. The Falcons released Jared Ivey and Drake Jackson in corresponding moves with Pearce's activation to the 53-man roster. Pearce's legal troubles early in the 2026 offseason resulted in a violation of the NFL's personal conduct policy, the league ruled. He was arrested on Feb. 7 following a domestic dispute with his then-girlfriend, Rickea Jackson, who stars for the WNBA's Chicago Sky. After his arrest, Pearce faced three felony charges: Aggravated battery with a deadly weapon, fleeing and eluding police and resisting an officer with violence to his or her person. He also faced a felony aggravated stalking charge, but that was later changed to a misdemeanor. A charge of aggravated battery of a law enforcement officer was dropped. "He's done everything that we've asked him, everything that he's been allowed to do," Stefanski said on Monday . "He's done a great job." Prolific Falcons pass rush should get even better Expectations for the Atlanta defensive front heading into the first half of the season were modest given Pearce's suspension and the loss of fellow edge rusher Jalon Walker for the year due to a torn ACL. The second-year players combined for 16 sacks as rookies, and Pearce finished third in Defensive Rookie of the Year voting. Fielding a defense without two young standouts figured to limit the Falcons' ability to pressure the pocket. Instead, they have done more than stay above water in that regard. Mayfield guided the Bucs to their second win of the season against the Carolina Panthers in Week 7, and oddsmakers are buying the Buccaneers at home in Week 8 against the Atlanta Falcons. The Buccaneers are favored to win their matchup with the Falcons, sitting as 2.5-point favorites in the odds at DraftKings Sportsbook . After a 1-5 start to the season, Tampa Bay's win over Carolina thrust it back into the mix to win the division this season. Another win over an NFC South opponent would go a long way for Tampa Bay getting into the playoffs, and the running game has really stepped forward in recent weeks with both Mayfield and Jalon Daniels under center. Mayfield wasn't asked to do much against Carolina, completing just seven of his 11 passes for 76 yards and a score. He's completed 63.6 percent of his passes for 679 yards, three scores and two picks in four games. Daniels led Tampa Bay to one win while Mayfield was sidelined, but it's pretty clear that oddsmakers view the former No. 1 overall pick as a major upgrade under center. Mayfield and the Bucs take on Altanta and Chicago over the next two weeks before their bye. Atlanta is currently one game ahead of Tampa Bay in the NFC South, but a win on Sunday would vault the Bucs into second in the divison, just a half-game back of the Panthers (3-4). (Injury Update, Betting Impact for Falcons vs. Buccaneers in NFL Week 8) Skip to main content ON SI Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield returned from a three-game absence due to a dislocated thumb in Week 7, and he's off the team's injury report and expected to play in Week 8. Mayfield guided the Bucs to their second win of the season against the Carolina Panthers in Week 7, and oddsmakers are buying the Buccaneers at home in Week 8 against the Atlanta Falcons. The Buccaneers are favored to win their matchup with the Falcons, sitting as 2.5-point favorites in the odds at DraftKings Sportsbook . After a 1-5 start to the season, Tampa Bay's win over Carolina thrust it back into the mix to win the division this season. Another win over an NFC South opponent would go a long way for Tampa Bay getting into the playoffs, and the running game has really stepped forward in recent weeks with both Mayfield and Jalon Daniels under center. Mayfield wasn't asked to do much against Carolina, completing just seven of his 11 passes for 76 yards and a score. He's completed 63.6 percent of his passes for 679 yards, three scores and two picks in four games. Daniels led Tampa Bay to one win while Mayfield was sidelined, but it's pretty clear that oddsmakers view the former No. 1 overall pick as a major upgrade under center. Mayfield and the Bucs take on Altanta and Chicago over the next two weeks before their bye. Atlanta is currently one game ahead of Tampa Bay in the NFC South, but a win on Sunday would vault the Bucs into second in the divison, just a half-game back of the Panthers (3-4). home.headline: Falcons starting lineups for Week 8 game vs. Tampa Bay Buccaneers
home.blurb: The Falcons are dealing with a few key injuries, but only one player has been officially ruled out. Running back Brian Robinson Jr. will miss his second game in a row due to a hamstring injury. However, eight other players have been given a questionable tag going into NFL Week 8. Linebacker Divine Deablo, cornerback A.J. Terrell, edge rusher Samson Ebukam, defensive back Billy Bowman Jr. and wide receiver Olamide Zaccheaus were all listed as questionable on the team's final Week 8 injury report . Check out the Falcons' starting linueps on offense, defense and special teams for Sunday's game in Tampa below. WR Olamide Zaccheaus ( Questionable ) ILB Divine Deablo ( Questionable ) NB Avieon Terrell ( Questionable ) KR Olamide Zaccheaus ( Questionable ) The Atlanta Falcons shocked the NFL world in Week 7 by defeating the previously unbeaten San Francisco 49ers, but their upcoming Week 8 matchup against the 2-5 Tampa Bay Buccaneers is perhaps even more important. While defeating a potential Super Bowl contender is a great accomplishment for Kevin Stefanski's team, the Falcons still must prove they can maintain that level of play from week to week. Sunday's game in Tampa is an opportunity for Atlanta to take control of the NFC South and show the NFL that this division has at least one respectable team. Robinson is the only player ruled out, but many are listed as questionable, including several key defenders. The Jaguars are set to host the Indianapolis Colts at EverBank Stadium in Week 8, with the Jaguars fresh off a bye and also playing at home for the first time since Week 3. With the Colts in complete teardown and rebuild mode, the Jaguars are clearly expected to roll past them this week, something head coach Liam Coen knows he has to be guarded against. "It's innate as a coach. I've been a part of it so many times, especially as an assistant where you're so hyper-focused on your group, like, ‘Hey, I hope my group plays well today. I hope my position plays well today.’ As a head coach in general, I hope we all play well, but I kind of expect us to. I do," Coen said Friday. "I don't expect us to walk out on the field and give lack of effort or guys not run to the football. And is it going to happen on some plays? Yeah. But as a whole, as a group, I do expect these guys to walk out on the field on Sunday and give their best effort for the most part. And is it always perfect? No. And that's what you're striving for, that perfect balance, but it's such an imperfect game. It is nice to know, this is the way I feel, that our guys are going to play on Sundays.” So, how does the national NFL media see the Jaguars and Colts matchup playing Sports Illustrated Albert Breer: Jaguars Eva Geitheim: Jaguars Mitch Goldich: Jaguars Mike Kadlick: Jaguars Gilbert Manzano: Jaguars Conor Orr: Jaguars John Pluym: Jauars Matt Verderame: Jaguars Pamela Maldonado: Jaguars Eric Moody: Jaguars Seth Walder: Jaguars Jeremy Bergman: Jaguars Brooke Cersosimo: Jaguars Gennaro Filice: Jaguars Bobby Kownack: Jaguars Dan Parr: Jaguars Joe Buscaglia: Jaguars Jon Greenberg: Jaguars Larry Holder: Jaguars Nick Kosmider: Jaguars Josh Kendal: Jaguars Austin Mock: Jaguars Jacksonville Jaguars On SI Analysis The Jaguars get a clean sweep here: 22 votes to 0. This isn't the first time the Jaguars have gotten this kind of vote, and it is worth noting that they have been able to prove the voters right each time they are seen as the big favorites, sans a close win against the Philadelphia Eagles. When the votes have been closer, such as in Week 2 and in Week 6, is when the Jaguars have found more trouble but that was never going to be the case here. I think the Colts are going to play hard. I think Shane Steichen is a solid coach. But I just think the Colts were a team that was already lacking the firepower to stack up with the Jaguars before it lost some of its best players. I ultimately expect an MVP-level performance from Trevor Lawrence, who matches up well against the Colts' defensive scheme and tendencies, and I also expect Daniel Jones to have a rough outing. Kickoff is set for 1:00 p.m. ET from EverBank Stadium in Jacksonville, Florida. The game will broadcast live on CBS. The Jaguars are 10.5-point favorites over the Colts on the spread, with the total set at over/under 46.5 points. Jacksonville is a -520 moneyline favorite to win outright, while Indianapolis is a +400 underdog to pull off the upset. Let's get into my Colts vs Jaguars prediction and player prop pick for today's game. Colts vs Jaguars pick: Bhayshul Tuten Over 64.5 Rushing Yards (-111) My Jaguars vs. Colts best bet is Bhayshul Tuten to record over 64.5 rushing yards. Make sure to find the best odds by checking our live NFL odds page. Colts vs Jaguars NFL Odds Colts vs Jaguars Spread : Colts +10.5 (-122), Jaguars -10.5 (+100) Colts vs Jaguars Total : over/under 45.5 (-106o / -114u) Colts vs Jaguars Moneyline : Colts +400, Jaguars -520 Colts vs Jaguars Preview for NFL Week 8 Indianapolis Colts Preview: Everything for Sale The fire sale is officially on in Indianapolis. Following a third consecutive loss, the Colts traded away Quenton Nelson ( Seahawks ) and DeForest Buckner ( 49ers ). Josh Downs has also requested a trade, while all eyes have shifted toward the team's prized possession: superstar running back Jonathan Taylor . For now, there are no expected changes at quarterback. Colts head coach Shane Steichen doubled down on Daniel Jones , who threw for just 108 yards last week. The veteran quarterback has struggled mightily this season, throwing more interceptions (7) than touchdowns (4) while posting a career-low completion rate of 59.6%. There is some positive news for Indianapolis, however. Tyler Warren is expected to return to the starting lineup after missing two games with a groin injury. The same goes for Sauce Gardner , while Downs will also suit up despite his trade request. Warren's presence is a must for a Colts receiving room that includes 34-year-old Keenan Allen and journeyman Laquon Treadwell . The question remains: Can the Colts weather the storm and put up a fight against their division rival? The biggest question is how the offensive line will hold up against a formidable Jaguars defense. Indianapolis ranks around league average in rushing yards per game, but those numbers came with Nelson anchoring the offensive line. Taylor is already averaging a career-low 4.2 yards per carry, and losing another key piece up front certainly won't help. The Colts defense has its own issues, ranking in the bottom 10 in points allowed per game and 11th in rushing yards allowed (124.4). Rush defense is definitely Indy's Achilles' heel on the defensive end, ranking 29th in rushing EPA allowed. The pass defense, however, has been surprisingly solid. Indianapolis hasn't allowed a wide receiver room to reach 100 receiving yards since Week 4, while opposing receivers are averaging just 10 receptions per game. Jacksonville Jaguars Preview: Bhayshul Tuten Due for Breakout Game It was a much-needed bye week for the Jaguars, who are coming off two London games filled with late-game theatrics. Jacksonville's defense has been its strong suit this season. Outside of the Texans (34 points), no team has scored more than 17 against this talented unit. The Jaguars rank No. 1 in rushing yards allowed per game (72.2) but have struggled mightily against the pass, ranking 30th while surrendering 274 yards per game. Ultimately, Jacksonville's success will hinge on Trevor Lawrence and the offense finding another gear. The Jaguars are around league average in total offensive production and have maintained a near 50-50 split between the passing and running games. I'd be surprised if Jacksonville's ground game doesn't start to take off soon as Bhayshul Tuten is on the verge of a breakout. The explosive running back possesses elite speed and has already shown the ability to rip off chunk plays. Unfortunately, several of those big gains have been wiped away by holding penalties. Still, Tuten has rushed for at least 65 yards in five of his six games this season. I've been waiting for this offense to take the next step, and there are plenty of weapons to make it happen. Outside of Tuten, Jacksonville has a talented receiving corps led by Parker Washington . We also saw Travis Hunter become more involved offensively before the bye, recording four catches for 59 yards and a touchdown. That increased usage is a trend I expect to continue in Week 8. Brian Thomas Jr. has also been the subject of trade speculation ahead of the upcoming deadline. He was benched for the second half against Houston and hasn't recorded a catch in either of Jacksonville's last two games, making his involvement worth watching. One situation worth monitoring is Jakobi Meyers , who enters Sunday questionable after missing Friday's practice with hamstring and ankle injuries. Thomas would likely be relied on to step up in his absence. Another development I've highlighted previously is Jacksonville's increased use of two-tight-end sets. Brenton Strange has been nothing short of excellent, but the emergence of Nate Boerkircher could be just as important moving forward. The second-round pick played a career-high 55% of the snaps before the bye, and I expect his workload to consistently settle in the 50–60% range. Colts vs Jaguars Picks, Betting Analysis I hinted at it earlier, but I expect the Jaguars' ground game to take off. To me, it's a matter of when, not if. Tuten is PFF's No. 1-ranked running back and ranks among the league's best in yards after contact per carry. He draws a Colts run defense that has struggled all season and will be without one of its most important defensive players in Buckner. With Jacksonville entering this matchup as a double-digit favorite, I expect the Jaguars to control possession and lean heavily on the ground game. That should mean a healthy workload for Tuten. Coming off a bye, Tuten should be fresh and ready to take advantage of a spiraling Colts squad. Don't be surprised if he finally breaks the 100-yard rushing mark in this one. away.headline: Jaguars HC Liam Coen confirms DaVon Hamilton, Eric Murray suffered season-ending injuries vs. Colts
away.blurb: Jacksonville Jaguars coach Liam Coen confirmed Monday that defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton and safety Eric Murray suffered season-ending injuries during Sunday’s 42-7 victory vs. the Indianapolis Colts. Hamilton sustained a torn quadriceps and left the field on a cart in the second quarter at EverBank Stadium. Murray injured his elbow on the opening kickoff. Neither player returned to the game after leaving the field. The losses leave the Jaguars without two defensive starters after improving to 5-2 and maintaining their lead in the AFC South. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport relayed Coen’s confirmation Monday on X, formerly Twitter, following his earlier report on Hamilton’s injury. Hamilton’s absence removes a vital piece of the NFL’s top rushing defense. Jacksonville has allowed just 77.4 rushing yards per game, with the veteran nose tackle helping control the middle of the line. Through seven games, Hamilton recorded 16 tackles, a half-sack, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery. The 29-year-old is in the final season of a three-year, $34.5 million extension signed in April 2023. Murray’s injury creates another opening in the secondary. The 32-year-old safety had 15 tackles in six starts after joining the Jaguars on a three-year, $19.5 million contract in 2025. Coen said both players will go on injured reserve in the coming days, forcing the Jaguars to adjust at two levels of its defense. The timing adds urgency ahead of the November 10 trade deadline. Jacksonville was already been exploring defensive-line help, and Hamilton’s absence increases that need as they try to protect their division lead without two experienced starters. away.blurb: Colts elevate CB Johnathan Edwards, DE Carl Lawson from practice squad to active roster Skip to main content Primary nav SCHEDULE The roster moves were made Saturday ahead Sunday's game against the Jaguars. The Indianapolis Colts today elevated cornerback Johnathan Edwards and defensive end Carl Lawson to the active roster from the practice squad for Sunday's game against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Edwards, 6-1, 201 pounds, has spent time on the team's active roster and practice squad this season. As a rookie in 2025, he played in 14 games (five starts) and registered 24 tackles (18 solo), three passes defensed and two special teams stops. Edwards was originally signed by the Colts as an undrafted free agent on May 9, 2025. Collegiately, he appeared in 45 career games at Tulane (2024) and Indiana State (2021-23) and recorded 124 tackles (86 solo), 1.5 tackles for loss, 22 passes defensed and one forced fumble. Lawson, 6-2, 260 pounds, was signed to the Indianapolis practice squad on October 7, 2026. He has played in 90 career games (34 starts) in his time with the Colts (2026), Baltimore Ravens (2025), Dallas Cowboys (2024), New York Jets (2022-23) and Cincinnati Bengals (2017-20). home.headline: Jacksonville Jaguars: Get devastating news on standout DT
home.blurb: The Jacksonville Jaguars blew out the Indianapolis Colts 42-7 on Sunday and are now 5-2 on the season. Unfortunately, the Jaguars couldn’t finish the game unscathed, as multiple players left with injuries. Standout defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton suffered an apparent knee injury during the second quarter and was carted off the field. During the postgame press conference, Liam Coen hinted that Hamilton suffered a significant injury as he reflected on his impact on the defense. “When he’s out there laying down and he’s reassuring me. That’s who he is. He’s reassuring me, and has a smile on his face, actually. He trusts God. He trusts himself. He trusts life. He’s just one of those types of people. Tough to see that, obviously.” “There’s not many better humans, better competitors, team guys,” Coen said, via Michael DiRocco of ESPN . “You should have saw D-Ham this week in practice. His leadership [with the] defensive line, individual periods this week, just the human, the competitor. I can’t say enough about him. The Jacksonville Jaguars get devastating news on standout DT According to Ian Rapoport, DaVon Hamilton suffered a torn quad and is expected to miss the rest of the season. This is devastating news for the Jaguars, especially since he’s a strong force behind the league’s top-ranked run defense . Hamilton (likely) finishes with 16 tackles, 13 stops , six pressures, a half sack, one forced fumble, and a fumble recovery across seven games. On top of that, the former third-round pick will become an unrestricted free agent in March, unless something happens contractually. Ruke Orhorhoro , Matt Dickerson , and third-round pick Albert Regis could take on expanded roles alongside starter Arik Armstead . Meanwhile, the Jaguars could be in the market for an interior defensive lineman ahead of next Tuesday’s NFL Trade Deadline. Notable candidates include Moro Ojomo , Grover Stewart , Zach Sieler, Christian Barmore, and Dalvin Tomlinson The post Jacksonville Jaguars: Get Devastating News on Standout DT appeared first on Gridiron Heroics .

picks.headline: Chargers vs. Rams bold predictions for NFL Week 8
picks.blurb: Chargers vs. Rams bold predictions for NFL Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football NFL Power Rankings Week 9 Waiver Wire Bears beat Seahawks MLB award finalists NBA Power Rankings Chargers vs. Rams bold predictions for NFL Week 8 Ben Strauss, ClutchPoints Thu, October 29, 2026 at 9:26 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The NFL teams based in Los Angeles are not having a great first half of the 2026 NFL season. Both the Chargers and Rams combined have three wins on the season headed into Week 8. The Rams are doing all of the heavy lifting here, but even they are having a disappointing season compared to their offseason expectations. It seems a Rams vs. Chargers Super Bowl is not in the cards this season. While both teams have been frustrating, they are in completely different situations ahead of Week 8. The Rams are very much alive in the NFC playoff race, but they need to continue stacking wins to remain competitive. Meanwhile, the Chargers are 0-6 and somehow still think they'll compete by the end of the season. This game means a lot for both teams, but the Rams arguably have much more to lose. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) So which team will come out on top in this one? Here are three bold predictions ahead of this Battle for Los Angeles in Week 8 between the Chargers and Rams. Rams, Chargers combine for more rushing yards than passing yards Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Both LA teams built their teams to have a strong running game. Jim Harbaugh is known for his love of pounding the rock. The Chargers drafted Omarion Hampton and built a massive offensive line for that very reason. As for the Rams, Sean McVay has always leaned heavily on the running game dating back to the Todd Gurley years. That has continued into 2026, as the Rams popularized 13 personnel usage and have taken to a new level this season. But just how committed are they to running the ball? When both teams combine their final stats, this game will feature more rushing yards than passing yards. That sounds like a crazy prediction on the surface. So exactly how bold is this prediction? The Rams average roughly 70 more passing yards than rushing yards per game this season, compared to an 82-yard gap for the Chargers. So it would be quite shocking if both teams overcame this 152-yard difference. If this happens, it may require both defenses to ball out against the pass and allow a handful of explosive runs. This is definitely bold, but crazier things have happened. The Chargers dominate the line of scrimmage on both sides of the ball If the Chargers are going to have a chance to win this game, they'll have to do so in the trenches. The injury situation for both teams makes this look like a strong possibility. Joe Alt is expected to return from injury for this game. One offensive lineman won't magically turn LA's o-line into an elite unit. However, it could do wonders as he still projects as an elite talent at the position. If the Chargers can count on one side of the line protected, they can always pull out some tricks to protect the other side. It is also important to note that the Rams have only managed 10 sacks in seven games played this season. That puts them at 27th in the NFL and only ahead of pitiful defensive teams like the Dolphins, Eagles, and Cowboys. It really shows that Myles Garrett, Kobie Turner, and Poona Ford are injured. Flipping to the other side, the Chargers and Rams look pretty evenly matched in the trenches. The Rams may hold a slight lead, but nothing too crazy. Ultimately, the Chargers' formula for winning this game is predicated on winning the trenches. This is certainly an area where they could gain an advantage. The Chargers will keep Justin Herbert completely clean, not allowing a single sack. Meanwhile, they will sack Matthew Stafford at least twice. That may not be a huge advantage, but it gives the Chargers a fighting chance. Chargers take Rams to overtime, but lose by a field goal Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images It is really tempting to predict that the Chargers will get their first win of the season in this spot. But it just seems too far-fetched. Realistically, the Rams and Chargers are in two completely different worlds on offense. The Rams average more total yards per game than any other team, while the Chargers are statistically a bottom five offense. There's no reason to suggest that will change in Week 8. Furthermore, the Rams absolutely must win this game to stay alive in the NFC playoff race. McVay may be willing to pull out all the stops if this game becomes close, and the Chargers would need to be lucky to survive in that situation. But playing for pride is important too, so the Chargers won't go down without a fight. They just don't have the horses to get the job done. Brandon McManus kicks a game-winning field goal in overtime, cementing himself as the Rams' kicker for the rest of the season. home.headline: Chargers Injury Report Ahead of Battle of LA Against Rams
home.blurb: With that said, health in this game is going to be critical, so let's take a look at the final injury report for the Chargers with players who are out, questionable, and on track to play. Additionally, Awosika, Thompson, and Leonard did not practice all week so head coach Jim Harbaugh and the coaching staff knew that they would be without those three players as well, which like James should not have affected the game plan too much. Lastly, for Mack to be available is not a surprise at all, as he was simply resting, and as a veteran, that is fairly normal for Mack so he should be a full go against the Rams' offensive line on Sunday. So, when the game starts on Sunday, it will be interesting to see if the Chargers can come out and have a full 60-minute performance to earn their first win of the year or if the Chargers' struggles will continue and lead to a Rams win as well as the Chargers falling to 0-7. More Videos The Los Angeles Chargers are hoping to earn their first win of the season on Sunday against the Los Angeles Rams in the battle of LA , but it will not be an easy task and will no doubt take a full 60-minute performance. WR Brenen Thompson (quadricep/hamstring) Focusing on James, he was actually placed on IR on Saturday, according to Adam Schefter , which is not really a surprise when considering that it was viewed as a possibility earlier in the week . As a result of that, the Chargers will now officially be without James for at least the next four games, which adds to the fact that James has not played since Week 3. So, the Chargers will need their safety room to step up with James being placed on IR. Now, looking at the big picture for Sunday, the Chargers knew they were more likely than not going to be without James, which should not affect their game plan too much on defense. In the secondary, it is going to be interesting to see if Jackson and Shelly are going to be able to play because the Rams have a great receiver in the form of Puka Nacua, who can take advantage if the secondary is not ready to play. On the offensive side, having Harris and McConkey being on track to be in the lineup for Sunday could be huge for quarterback Justin Herbert and the offense to get on track in the passing game which is something that the offense has been unable to do all year thus far. All that said, the Chargers are in a solid position health wise heading into this matchup against the Rams, so it will ultimately come downs to which team executes better between the Chargers and the Rams.

home.headline: Chargers Injury Report: No changes from Bolts’ 2nd day of Rams prep
home.blurb: Offensive guard Kayode Awosika (fibula) and wide receiver Brenen Thompson (quad/hamstring) were once again non-participants. There was hope both could return this week, but they're slated to miss yet another week at this rate. Receivers Ladd McConkey (concussion) and Tre' Harris (hamstring) were full and limited, respectively. Having Harris back out there will be huge for the offense, but recent history tells us we can't be confident in McConkey's return lasting all that long. Cornerback Rodney Shelley is on pace to return from a hamstring injury and the Chargers will need him with fellow corner Deane Leonard still rehabbing a concussion. Veteran Donte Jackson returning to the field would also be huge for the cornerback room that continues to be wiped out by injuries. home.headline: Two Key Chargers Players Will Return to Action in Week 8 Versus the Rams
home.blurb: Two Key Chargers Players Will Return to Action in Week 8 Versus the Rams - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Two Key Chargers Players Will Return to Action in Week 8 Versus the Rams Safety Derwin James Jr. remains out with a hamstring injury. This week, he reportedly had a setback, and as a result, head coach Jim Harbaugh said he's a candidate to go on injured reserve. Left guard Kayode Awosika (fibula), wide receiver Brenen Thompson (quad/hamstring) and cornerback Deane Leonard (concussion) also won't play. Cornerbacks Donte Jackson and Rodney Shelley, both of whom have hamstring injuries, are questionable for Sunday's contest. Garrett will be out on Sunday, as will wide receiver Davante Adams. At times, the Rams have struggled defensively — they gave up 302 passing yards last week against the Las Vegas Raiders — so perhaps there is a slight opening for the Bolts to find some success. Robert Marvi Sat, October 31, 2026 at 2:00 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads There isn't a whole lot the Los Angeles Chargers can do right now, or even by the end of the season, to play a lot better. The most immediate thing that would help is for them to become healthier. Starting right tackle Joe Alt hasn't played since Week 4 against the Seattle Seahawks due to a neck injury. Wide receiver Ladd McConkey suffered a concussion during L.A.'s last game, which was a 22-6 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 6, and he entered concussion protocol as a result. Both men returned to practice for the Chargers this week, and there is good news about their status for this Sunday's game against the Los Angeles Rams. Alt and McConkey are on the mend In the Chargers' final injury report for Sunday's game, neither Alt nor McConkey are listed, which means both are expected to play, per Noah Furtado of The Athletic. While the Chargers are 0-6 and have been a disaster, the Rams haven't exactly lived up to expectations either. The Rams have a 3-4 record despite being strong favorites to win the Super Bowl championship when the season started, and while they have had some injuries, such as the one that reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett is dealing with, they have their own problems. The Bolts currently rank last in the NFL in points per game, 28th in passing yards and last in turnovers. Quarterback Justin Herbert is tied for the most interceptions heading into Week 8 with eight, against just five touchdown passes. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 8 picks, including the Bills to top the Ravens in a high-scoring game Getty Images Going to the dogs last week turned out to be dog doodoo. I picked every dog against the spread last week and it looked good early, but then it collapsed late with five straight losses, including both prime-time games Sunday and Monday night. I was 8-6 straight up last week and 6-7-1 against the spread. Hey, the spread record was an improvement, which tells you how bad I've been this season. My ATS record this year is 43-61-3, which is a long way from .500. My straight-up record is 62-44-1. So this week, it's back to just picking the games. Forget all dogs. Trying to get to .500 makes me borrow a coaching cliché they all use. One game at a time. One week at a time. Turnaround time. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Lamar Jackson could be back for the Ravens, but how much will his injured ankle impact his ability to move? The Bills are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. Baltimore's defense was bad in the loss to the Bengals last week, but Buffalo's defense has been awful. Look for a shootout here with Josh Allen getting the best of it. Pick: Bills 35, Ravens 30 Tennessee Titans at Cincinnati Bengals (-10.5) The Titans are having major problems on offense, while the Bengals lit up the Ravens last week. Joe Burrow was special in the second half of that game and I think that will carry over here. Look for an offensive explosion from the Bengals as Burrow starts to get into the MVP talk. Pick: Bengals 36, Titans 10 Arizona Cardinals at Dallas Cowboys (-6.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Cowboys' offense came alive against the Eagles Monday night, especially on the ground, which isn't a good thing for an Arizona defense that is last in the league in scoring. The Dallas offense should roll and the Arizona offense won't be able to keep up. Dallas big — even on a short week. Pick: Cowboys 37, Cardinals 21 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) The undefeated Vikings face a tough road game here against Detroit. The Lions offense against the Minnesota defense will be a treat to watch. Jared Goff is playing at a high level right now, but Minnesota's defense is the best in the league in terms of scoring. The Vikings offense is limited, but the Detroit defense has had major problems. But they were better last week, which I think carries over. Lions take it. Pick: Lions 23, Vikings 13 Las Vegas Raiders at New York Jets (-1.5) Kirk Cousins stays in as the starter for the Raiders, but teams have blitzed him the past two weeks. That could be a problem here since the Jets are a top-10 team in blitz percentage. The Raiders have struggled to stop opposing offenses, giving up 28.1 points per game, so look for Geno Smith to have success. Jets win it. Pick: Jets 27, Raiders 16 Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) This is a big game for the division lead in the AFC North. The Browns beat the Steelers earlier this year, but this will be a bigger challenge on the road. They are also playing consecutive road games, which will be a challenge. Look for Aaron Rodgers to play well as the Steelers take it. Pick: Steelers 24, Browns 20 Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (-2.5) This is suddenly a big game in the NFC South with the Bucs upsetting Carolina last week and the Falcons upsetting the 49ers. The Tampa Bay running game has come alive, but Atlanta is stingy on the ground, giving up 3.8 per rush. That will mean this is a Baker Mayfield game. Tampa Bay gives up 3.5 per rush, which might make for tough going for Bijan Robinson. That's a problem for the Atlanta offense. Tampa Bay wins it. Pick: Bucs 23, Falcons 17 Indianapolis Colts at Jacksonville Jaguars (-9.5) The Colts are a mess; they are playing consecutive road games, and they haven't won at Jacksonville since 2014, when Andrew Luck was the quarterback. Oh, and they traded their best offensive lineman, Quentin Nelson. The Jaguars are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. This one will get ugly as the Jaguars bounce back from the loss to the Texans in London. Pick: Jaguars 30, Colts 16 Los Angeles Chargers (+6.5) at Los Angeles Rams Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The battle of Los Angeles isn't quite the game many expected before the season. The Chargers, coming off a bye, haven't won yet and the Rams have been a disappointment. But the Rams won last week at Las Vegas to seemingly right things. They will win here, but the rested Chargers will keep it close. Pick: Rams 23, Chargers 20 Kansas City Chiefs (-1.5) at Denver Broncos Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Chiefs' offense was lifeless in Seattle on Sunday night and now faces a tough Denver defense. They have to find ways to get the running game going again with Kenneth Walker. Bo Nix showed some life last week in the victory over Arizona, but this Chiefs defense will be a challenge. Look for a low-scoring game won by Kansas City, with Walker getting going against Denver's defense, which gives up 4.6 yards per rush. Pick: Chiefs 19, Broncos 14 New England Patriots (-7) at Miami Dolphins The Dolphins won their first game last week and have been in a lot of their losses. But this New England team will be a challenge, even at home. The Patriots are coming off a bad road loss to the Bears, and they will be rested, having played on Thursday. The defense limits the Dolphins' offense, and Drake Maye will play well. New England wins it. Pick: Pats 28, Dolphins 14 Philadelphia Eagles at Washington Commanders (-5.5) Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This might be an elimination game of sorts for these two. Both need a victory in the worst way — even in their horrible division. The Eagles are crippled by injuries, but Washington has plenty of their own. With the Eagles on a short week off a Monday night game and the Commanders off a bye, Washington will win it. Pick: Commanders 28, Eagles 16 Chicago Bears at Seattle Seahawks (-3) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are riding high behind Caleb Williams and an improved defense. But this is a tough road trip against a Seattle team that showed what it can do on defense by shutting down the Chiefs Sunday night. Seattle also got the running game going. The Seattle defense will slow down the Chicago offense, and the Seahawks will win it. Pick: Seahawks 24, Bears 17 Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime These two are both coming off losses. The Carolina loss featured the Bucs running over them for 258 rushing yards. It's been a problem all year. But the Packers don't run it very well, so something has to give. Carolina gave Jordan Love fits last year, but that will change here. Carolina gives up 27.7 points per game. Love lights them up and Josh Jacobs gets the run game going.
