Replicating that performance is going to be much easier said than done in the rematch, however, especially with Andy Reid's team hitting the road. Denver seems to be finding its stride just a little bit, although a win over the Arizona Cardinals won't convince anyone that the reigning division champions are all the way back. The winner of Sunday's tilt could generate some serious momentum in the AFC West race as the season approaches its midpoint. What gives in the afternoon window of play? The Kansas City Chiefs On SI crew makes its predictions for Week 8 of the regular season. Joshua Brisco: For the second week in a row, I'm expecting a low-scoring game. This time, however, I think the Chiefs will find the end zone. Kansas City just needs enough from Rashee Rice and his fellow pass catchers to allow Kenneth Walker to have opportunities similar to the ones he took advantage of in Week 1. The final inactives list will be massive for both teams, but I expect the Chiefs to escape Denver with a narrow win. Jordan Foote: Getting wideout Rashee Rice back in the fold for this one is huge. Given that Xavier Worthy's come back down to earth, Travis Kelce is banged up and Kenneth Walker III has finally looked human, having a formidable weapon on offense is paramount. On the other side of the ball, missing cornerback Mansoor Delane will hurt, but being minus L'Jarius Sneed might just be an addition-by-subtraction scenario. Expect a one-score game that is far from the prettiest, albeit with Kansas City still doing enough to complete the sweep of Denver and maintain first place in the AFC West. Joshua Schulman: The Chiefs are reeling after an ugly loss to Seattle in prime time last week. It’s difficult to imagine the offense looking any more inept than it did a week ago when it mustered just one field goal all night. The Broncos’ defense isn’t quite as dominant as Seattle’s but still is a formidable unit. With that said, we saw who the better team was when these two sides met in Week 1. Denver has been winning in spite of Bo Nix’s play, not because of it, and the KC coaching staff has to have stressed the importance of a game in which it could lose the first-place lead in the AFC West. Tyler Brown: This feels like a tighter game than Week 1, but the Chiefs' strengths match up well against those of the Broncos. Denver will be desperate with the divisional stakes swinging so heavily. With Jonathan Cooper lined up opposite Nik Bonitto, the Broncos have a better edge-rush pairing than they did in September, which puts the Chiefs’ tackle situation under real stress if it ends up in too many obvious dropback situations. The Broncos may perform better this go-around, but the matchup tilts toward the Chiefs. Denver’s rushing defense ranks 28th and leads the league in missed tackles, which is exactly the situation Kenneth Walker thrives in. Getting Rashee Rice back is a bigger deal than it may sound, because it gives Patrick Mahomes another reliable weapon and it lets Xavier Worthy and the rest of the group settle into their roles. On the other side, Denver is 30th in total offense and 25th in scoring, and Nix has struggled when pressured, especially against the blitz. If Steve Spagnuolo gets creative and some pass rushers outside of George Karlaftis step up, that is another major Chiefs advantage. The Chiefs are still 5-1 this season, but they scored just three points in their last game and failed to reach the red zone on a single possession. Will a Denver defense that has been red hot in recent weeks be able to slow down Kenneth Walker III and this Chiefs attack? away.headline: Chiefs dealt double injury blow before facing Broncos
away.blurb: The Chiefs won the first meeting between the two teams in Week 1, demolishing the Broncos 31-10. But Denver has responded well since then, and now has the opportunity to move ahead of their division rivals in the standings. With the Broncos’ defense allowing just 18.3 points per game since Week 2, Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs’ offense will have their work cut out for them. Unfortunately, Kansas City’s defense now won’t have two of their best players. Rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane has been downgraded to out with a shoulder injury after being listed as questionable on Friday’s injury report, while veteran corner L’Jarius Sneed has been placed on injured reserve because of a knee injury. Sneed will miss at least the next four games, leaving the Chiefs without two important members of their secondary against Denver. Sneed is also dealing with a recurring injury, with the knee issue forcing him to be limited in practice on Thursday and Friday. But his being placed on IR clearly signals the injury is more serious than anticipated, with Week 12 viewed as his expected return date. In six appearances this season, Sneed has recorded 32 combined tackles (22 solo), three pass breakups, two forced fumbles, and one fumble recovery. The Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos will meet for an important AFC West showdown on Sunday, with the division lead on the line. Kansas City enters at 5-1 after suffering their first loss of the NFL season in Seattle last weekend, while Denver is 5-2 and riding a three-game winning streak after beating the Cardinals in Arizona. More news : Jonathan Taylor Trade Talks Heat Up as Colts Change Their Stance Delane, the Chiefs’ sixth overall pick, initially injured his right shoulder during the offseason and aggravated it in the season opener against Denver. After returning to the lineup in Week 3, he suffered another setback during Wednesday’s practice ahead of the rematch with Denver. In five games this season, Delane has recorded 27 combined tackles (17 solo), three tackles for loss, five pass breakups, and one interception. He’s also played nearly every defensive snap since returning in Week 3. More news : NFL to Review New Allegations Against Packers Star Josh Jacobs More news : Jets Send Clear Message on Garrett Wilson Amid Trade Buzz Losing both players is a tough blow to Kansas City’s secondary, particularly against a division rival that’s found its rhythm over the past few weeks. Delane has become the Chiefs’ primary shutdown corner, while Sneed provides experience and flexibility to move around the defensive backfield. Kristian Fulton and Nohl Williams should likely see expanded roles in the meantime. The timing is also less than ideal considering the Chiefs’ upcoming schedule. After the Broncos on Sunday, Kansas City will host the Jets before traveling to face the Falcons and hosting the Cardinals. away.headline: Broncos injuries: Brandon Jones aggravated hamstring vs. Chiefs
away.blurb: Broncos safety Brandon Jones, who injured his hamstring last Thursday and was listed as questionable on Friday's injury report, started Sunday's game against the Kansas City Chiefs and totaled three tackles in the first half before aggravating his injury. Jones was ruled out at halftime, leaving Taylor Rapp, Devon Key and JL Skinner to handle safety duties with Talanoa Hufanga ( ankle ) already sidelined. The Denver Broncos pulled off yet another comeback win on Sunday, but it came at a cost. It was always a risk to have Jones play in Sunday's game after he tweaked his hamstring in practice this week. Now, the injury could be worse, and it's not uncommon for hamstring injuries to sideline players for multiple weeks. There's been no word yet on the severity of Jones' aggravated injury, but it wouldn't be shocking if he misses Sunday's game against the Carolina Panthers given the nature of hamstring injuries. After that, Denver has a bye in Week 10. Elsewhere on the injury front, wide receiver Courtland Sutton was shaken up in the second quarter after an 18-yard catch and went into the team's blue medical tent, but he later returned to the game. Broncos cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine also suffered an ankle injury in the second quarter but returned in the second half. Social : Follow Broncos Wire on Facebook and Twitter/X ! away.headline: Injury Report: CB Pat Surtain II not assigned game status, 4 Broncos listed as questionable for Week 8 game vs. Chiefs
away.blurb: Injury Report: CB Pat Surtain II not assigned game status, 4 Broncos listed as questionable for Week 8 game vs. Chiefs Skip to main content Primary nav Game Day ENGLEWOOD, Colo. — Cornerback Pat Surtain II appears poised to return to the field for the Broncos. Surtain (ankle) was a full participant for the third consecutive practice, and he was not assigned a game status for Sunday's matchup against the Chiefs. The absence of a game status indicates Surtain will be available to play. While Surtain is expected to make his return, four Broncos are listed as questionable to play in Sunday's game. Defensive lineman Zach Allen (hamstring), tackle Garett Bolles (hip), safety Brandon Jones (hamstring) and wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (chest) are questionable for the division matchup. All four players were limited in Friday's practice. Running back RJ Harvey (knee) — who was added the Broncos' injury report on Thursday — and safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) were both ruled out. Harvey did not practice on Friday after he was limited on Thursday. All four Broncos who were listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Chiefs are active for the Week 8 game. The Broncos' All-Pro cornerback suffered his injury against the 49ers in Week 4. Wide receiver Marvin Mims Jr. (ankle), inside linebacker Karene Reid (elbow) and defensive tackle Malcolm Roach (neck) were all full participants on Friday and also not assigned game statuses. away.headline: Chiefs’ Week 8 injury report vs. Broncos: Is Travis Kelce’s ankle injury something to worry about?
away.blurb: Kelce had been nursing an ankle injury this week, and he was a limited participant in practice on Thursday. The good news is that he was a full participant on Wednesday and Friday, which was good news for his status against the Broncos. Chiefs’ Week 8 injury report vs. Broncos: Is Travis Kelce’s ankle injury something to worry about? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Malik Brown, ClutchPoints Sun, November 1, 2026 at 4:42 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Kansas City Chiefs were able to take care of business against the Denver Broncos at the beginning of the season, and they'll be looking to do the same thing in Week 8. Things could be a little different this time, as the Chiefs had been dealing with some injuries during the week, one of which happened to be Travis Kelce 's issue. It doesn't seem as if there's anything to worry about regarding Kelce, as he doesn't have an injury designation ahead of the game. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Kelce is still making an impact on the field, and though they lost to the Seattle Seahawks last week, he finished with 44 yards. That's about the amount of yards that he's averaging this season, which isn't bad for him. In their first matchup against the Broncos this season, Kelce finished with 71 yards. The hope is that he can have that same production this time around, especially as they face one of the best defenses in the league. The Chiefs also seem to be in the business of improving their offense, and they're in the market for a wide receiver , according to NFL insider James Palmer. "The Kansas City Chiefs, to my understanding, have been working the phones for weeks here trying to get a wide receiver for Patrick Mahomes. Is that Brian Thomas Jr.? Is that Josh Downs? They've been kind of weighing their options. (Chiefs General Manager) Brett Veach has done this before. We'll see if he can do it again before the deadline," Palmer said. away.headline: Kansas City Chiefs' first injury report for Week 8 vs. Denver Broncos sees some very important players returning to practice
away.blurb: Everyone participated in practice in some capacity on Wednesday, just as Chiefs HC Andy Reid said they would . The team ran a light 10-10-10 practice to start the week before ramping up with pads on Thursday and Friday. Returning to the lineup was WR Rashee Rice, who missed the past two games with a hamstring injury. Additionally, starting RT Jaylon Moore returned after missing Week 7 with a concussion. The other player back at practice? Chiefs second-year DT Omarr Norman-Lott. He was designated to return to practice after missing over 365 days with an ACL injury. KEY: DNP = Did not participate | LP = Limited participation | FP = Full participation | NIR = Not injury related Rashee Rice and Omarr Norman-Lott were both limited on a light practice day. I expect Rice to ramp up a bit more on Thursday, while Norman-Lott will likely ease back in after not practicing for over 12 months. Pat Surtain II's full participation on Wednesday is a positive sign that he'll return to action in Week 8 after missing multiple weeks with an ankle injury. home.blurb: Allen went down in the fourth quarter of last Sunday's 30-16 win over the Arizona Cardinals and appeared to be favoring his right hamstring. He was able to walk off the field into the team's blue medical tent, but did not return to the game. Allen finished the game standing on the sideline without his helmet as Denver closed out a win. After the game, Allen was asked about the injury and said, "Yeah, I'll be fine. Yeah, I'll be good." He was listed as questionable for today's game on Friday's injury report. Allen (and all of the players listed as questionable) are active and set to play against the Chiefs today. Denver Broncos defensive lineman Zach Allen ( hamstring ) is active for Sunday's game against the Kansas City Chiefs. Allen has been one of the best interior defensive linemen in the NFL this season, totaling 24 tackles, 19 quarterback hits, 4.5 sacks, two pass breakups and one forced fumble through seven games. He's well on his way toward earning another first-team All-Pro nod after securing the first such honor of his career last season. The Broncos ' defensive line rotation this season has been led by Allen ( 343 snaps ), Malcolm Roach ( 283 ), Eyioma Uwazurike ( 272 ) and D.J. Jones ( 220 ). Surtain (ankle) was a full participant for the third consecutive practice, and he was not assigned a game status for Sunday's matchup against the Chiefs. The absence of a game status indicates Surtain will be available to play. While Surtain is expected to make his return, four Broncos are listed as questionable to play in Sunday's game. home.headline: Chiefs’ Week 8 injury report vs. Broncos: Is Travis Kelce’s ankle injury something to worry about?
home.blurb: Kelce had been nursing an ankle injury this week, and he was a limited participant in practice on Thursday. The good news is that he was a full participant on Wednesday and Friday, which was good news for his status against the Broncos. Chiefs’ Week 8 injury report vs. Broncos: Is Travis Kelce’s ankle injury something to worry about? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Malik Brown, ClutchPoints Sun, November 1, 2026 at 4:42 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Kansas City Chiefs were able to take care of business against the Denver Broncos at the beginning of the season, and they'll be looking to do the same thing in Week 8. Things could be a little different this time, as the Chiefs had been dealing with some injuries during the week, one of which happened to be Travis Kelce 's issue. It doesn't seem as if there's anything to worry about regarding Kelce, as he doesn't have an injury designation ahead of the game. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Kelce is still making an impact on the field, and though they lost to the Seattle Seahawks last week, he finished with 44 yards. That's about the amount of yards that he's averaging this season, which isn't bad for him. In their first matchup against the Broncos this season, Kelce finished with 71 yards. The hope is that he can have that same production this time around, especially as they face one of the best defenses in the league. The Chiefs also seem to be in the business of improving their offense, and they're in the market for a wide receiver , according to NFL insider James Palmer. "The Kansas City Chiefs, to my understanding, have been working the phones for weeks here trying to get a wide receiver for Patrick Mahomes. Is that Brian Thomas Jr.? Is that Josh Downs? They've been kind of weighing their options. (Chiefs General Manager) Brett Veach has done this before. We'll see if he can do it again before the deadline," Palmer said. It's been a largely disappointing first half of the season for wide receiver A.J. Brown in his debut campaign with the New England Patriots . Things are possibly about to get worse for the Patriots and their marquee offseason trade acquisition. New England could potentially afford to sit Brown in Week 8 if he's not healthy enough, as the Patriots are heavy road favorites for Sunday's contest versus the Miami Dolphins. New England has a pair of NFC North contenders on deck in Weeks 9 and 10 with the Green Bay Packers and Detroit Lions, respectively, before its Week 11 bye. The Patriots are just 4-3 this fall, however, so if they want to make a run at their second straight AFC East crown and put pressure on the Buffalo Bills (5-1), they can't take the Dolphins for granted. Brown has played in just three of New England's first seven contests this year as he missed Weeks 2, 3, 4 and 5 due to a high-ankle sprain. The three-time Pro Bowler returned to action in Week 6 against the New York Jets but has yet to have an impact on offense. Brown has played only 132 offensive snaps in his three games and has recorded nine catches for 101 scoreless yards on 20 targets. His longest reception of the season has gone for just 18 yards, but Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said on Monday that he isn't concerned about the 29-year-old's lack of production. Thursday's news still leaves the door open for Brown to take the field and perhaps turn things around on Sunday, but it's not looking great.

Brown as questionable to play due to knee and ankle injuries. Both players did not participate in practice on Thursday or Friday. Per ESPN’s Adam Schefter, the Patriots downgraded Brown and Henderson to out on Saturday. Brown suffered a high-ankle sprain in the Patriots’ Week 1 loss to the Seattle Seahawks that kept him out until New England played the New York Jets in Week 6. On Friday, Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said the knee injury Brown is dealing with this week is separate from the high-ankle sprain injury he suffered against Seattle. He wasn’t able to finish practice on Wednesday. “Just like everything else, when you come out of the game or a long week or practice on Monday, you evaluate the player,” Vrabel said , via the Patriots’ website. “He just wasn’t able to practice or finish practice on Wednesday. away.blurb: The New England Patriots are gearing up for a vital AFC East matchup against the Miami Dolphins while facing significant roster changes. Wide receiver A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) and running back TreVeyon Henderson (illness) have both been ruled out for the game. As a result, quarterback Drake Maye will need to rely on depth players such as DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism III, Kyle Williams, and tight end Hunter Henry to keep the offense functioning. Initially, the growing number of absences forced fantasy managers and analysts to look for replacements. However, head coach Mike Vrabel provided some clarity during his recent media availability. Reports from Mike Reiss and Karen Guregian on social media highlighted several key injury updates. Reiss noted that when Vrabel was asked about A.J. Brown’s status, the head coach replied, “We’ll see how he progresses through the week.” In addition, Guregian said wide receiver Mack Hollins could be activated off injured reserve this week, which would significantly bolster a depleted receiving corps. However, concerning tight end Hunter Henry’s foot injury, Guregian mentioned that Vrabel had no updates , indicating that Henry’s game-day status would depend on his response to treatment. As New England navigates these ongoing injury challenges, monitoring the progress of Brown, Hollins, and Henry in practice will be crucial for both the Patriots’ game plan and fantasy managers adjusting their lineups for Week 8. home.blurb: Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown and running back TreVeyon Henderson have been ruled out for Sunday's game at Miami. Brown and Henderson were among those listed as questionable on the team's injury report Friday. Brown hurt his knee during Wednesday's practice, after which he was listed with knee and ankle injuries for the first time this season. He did not practice Thursday or Friday. At running back, Rhamondre Stevenson and Corey Kiner are expected to take most, if not all, of the carries, while Larison contributes primarily on special teams. On Friday, Patriots coach Mike Vrabel expressed optimism the team could replace any players who might be out in Miami. On Saturday, the Patriots also ruled out backup offensive tackle Marcus Bryant, who has been designated to return off injured reserve but not activated to the 53-man roster. Cornerback Carlton Davis (neck) and linebacker Christian Elliss (chest) are still listed as questionable for kickoff, though Davis has indicated he expects to play for the first time in three weeks. home.headline: Injury Report Analysis: WR A.J. Brown, RB TreVeyon Henderson questionable for Week 8 matchup vs. the Dolphins
home.blurb: Injury Report Analysis: WR A.J. Brown, RB TreVeyon Henderson questionable for Week 8 matchup vs. the Dolphins Skip to main content Primary nav NEWS Brown (ankle/knee) is officially questionable for Sunday's game after sitting out the final two practices this week. On Friday, New England listed WR A.J. Brown (ankle/knee), RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness), CB Carlton Davis III (neck), and LB Christian Elliss (chest) as questionable for Week 8. On the one hand, the Patriots haven't ruled out any players as their active roster gets healthier. However, several key contributors remain on injured reserve (WR Mack Hollins, WR Romeo Doubs, LG Aijah Vera-Tucker, RG Mike Onwenu), while Brown's participation decreasing as the practice week wore on was a noteworthy development. While still managing his recovery from a high-ankle sprain, Brown's knee reportedly "flared up" in practice this week, which landed him on Wednesday's injury report as limited. Brown then didn't participate in Thursday or Friday's session, but the 29-year-old still has a chance to play on Sunday. The Pats top wideout has caught just 6-of-16 targets for 75 receiving yards in two games since returning from injury. On Friday, head coach Mike Vrabel had an update on Brown's status. As for the offensive line, the Patriots are managing injuries there, too. Starting RT Morgan Moses continues to play through a foot injury while C/G Ben Brown is pushing to get back into the lineup. Brown started three games at right guard before exiting the Patriots Week 6 win over the Jets with a knee injury. Brown was a full participant in practice this week, suggesting he could return to the starting lineup. Moving over to the defense, the positive injury news is that the Patriots secondary is expected to be whole for the first time since Week 3. Although he's officially questionable, CB Carlton Davis III (neck) is trending toward playing on Sunday after participating in full for all three practices this week. Davis has missed three straight games and four of the last six contests due to his neck injury, while top CB Christian Gonzalez has also missed time with a shoulder injury. "Yeah, I mean, it's everything," Gonzalez said of Davis's return. "CD is a great vet. Somebody that I lean on a lot, able to talk to, pick his mind about certain things. He's seen a lot of balls, so just having him back out there is amazing. Excited to get all of us back." Although the wide receiver situation is in flux, the Patriots roster health is trending in the right direction, with OL Ben Brown and CB Carlton Davis III expected to return this week. The next steps for New England are practice squad elevations and downgrades en route to Miami on Saturday. As mentioned, the Pats could elevate a practice-squad receiver due to Brown's uncertain status, with Dixon or Dorner as frontrunners, or practice-squad RB Lan Larison to fill in for Henderson – we'll keep you updated. news Injury Report Analysis: Patriots rule out five play

away.headline: Eagles missing Saquon Barkley, 2 starting WRs at Thursday's practice
away.blurb: The Philadelphia Inquirer's Zach Berman noted the limited depth, suggesting that another roster addition might have been expected if Barkley were in serious danger of missing Sunday's game. However, not making another move does not guarantee Barkley will be available against Washington. None of the three has been ruled out for Sunday, but their continued absence from practice makes Friday's final injury report especially important. The Philadelphia Eagles could be without several important offensive contributors for Sunday's matchup against the Washington Commanders , with running back Saquon Barkley and wide receivers DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks absent from the portion of Thursday's practice open to reporters. ESPN's Tim McManus and Olivia Reiner said all three players were missing as Philadelphia began its first full practice of the week after Monday night's 38-21 loss to the Dallas Cowboys. The absences are particularly concerning because the team listed all three players as nonparticipants on Wednesday's estimated injury report. Philadelphia held a walkthrough Wednesday, so the participation designations were projections rather than based on actual practice activity. Philadelphia Eagles Barkley continues to deal with hamstring and back injuries after leaving Monday's loss to Dallas. The veteran returned against the Cowboys after missing two games with a hamstring issue, but his back tightened during the contest, eventually forcing him to the sideline. His absence Thursday adds to uncertainty in an Eagles backfield already depleted by injuries. Philadelphia placed Dameon Pierce on injured reserve Wednesday, leaving Elijah Mitchell and Jaydon Blue as the only other running backs on the active roster. Pierce emerged as a key contributor during Barkley's previous absence, leading the team's running backs with 151 offensive snaps over seven games. The Eagles promoted Blue from the practice squad Wednesday, but they haven't added another running back to the active roster. Philadelphia also continues to monitor Smith and Wicks, who missed Monday night's loss because of hamstring and ankle injuries, respectively. Their absences have put additional responsibility on rookie Makai Lemon, who caught his first career touchdown against Dallas, and the remaining members of the receiving corps. For Tanner McKee, losing multiple offensive playmakers would create another significant challenge as the Eagles try to end their five-game losing streak. Philadelphia enters Week 8 averaging just 18.1 points per game, ranking near the bottom of the NFL in scoring. Losing Barkley and two established receiving options would further limit an offense struggling to sustain drives. The Eagles' official Thursday injury report will provide more clarity on Barkley, Smith, and Wicks' participation levels. away.headline: Eagles legend makes bold prediction for NFL season after Commanders loss
away.blurb: The team has been relying on backup quarterback Tanner McKee with Jalen Hurts out for the season, recovering from his diagnosis of deep vein thrombosis in his leg and bilateral pulmonary emboli in his lungs. McKee threw for over 200 passing yards but couldn’t find any receivers in the end zone, as Barkley had the Eagles’ only touchdown all game. Along with that, the Eagles have games against the Seattle Seahawks, San Francisco 49ers, and then a rematch against the Giants to close out their regular season. It’s been a difficult season for the Philadelphia Eagles , who suffered their sixth straight loss Sunday night against the Washington Commanders, 27-10. The loss came with star running back Saquon Barkley attempting to help his team amid his lingering hamstring issue. Along with that, they were still without their starting receivers, DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks, due to injuries. Although their season has been hampered by a series of unfortunate circumstances, including injuries to key players, one Eagles legend still believes in them as a team. Former Eagles quarterback Donovan McNabb recently expressed optimism about Philadelphia’s playoff chances despite the team’s ongoing struggles. More news: Ravens Star Under Fire for What He Said After Lamar Jackson Injury vs Bills “I think we can make the playoffs,” McNabb said while speaking on Sports Radio 94WIP , also adding, “It doesn’t matter what your record is: If it’s nine, seven, or eight. You win in the NFC East, and you get in, and anything can happen.” McNabb was reminded that McKee is currently Philadelphia’s starting quarterback, but he still gave him the benefit of the doubt when it comes to the Eagles salvaging their season. “I would stick with Tanner definitely for the next three weeks and see where that leads us,” the Eagles legend said, adding, “I don’t think there’s a desperate need to make a change now for someone who just got there.” While speaking with Kay Adams for “ Up & Adams with Kay Adams ,” McNabb indicated that he thinks the winner of the upcoming Eagles-Giants Week 9 game will win the NFC East. That game occurs on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 1 p.m. ET in Philadelphia, giving the home team a chance to snap their losing streak. The Eagles are currently 2-6, while the Giants lead the division with a 4-2-1 record. The 3-5 Dallas Cowboys haven’t done themselves any favors when it comes to trying to win the division, as they squandered a home game against the Cardinals on Sunday and lost on a field goal in overtime. Meanwhile, the Commanders improved to 2-4-1 by defeating the Eagles, giving Jayden Daniels and Washington a chance at the division if they can use this momentum. If Philadelphia hopes to win the division and reach the playoffs, it might need to pull off some upsets over some challenging opponents on its remaining schedule. They’ll get a bye week after the Giants game before traveling to Pittsburgh to face Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers on Sunday, Nov. 22. More news: Saquo

away.headline: Eagles at Commanders Injury Report
away.blurb: RB Saquon Barkley against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 7 action After not practicing on Wednesday and Thursday with hamstring and back injuries, Saquon Barkley practiced in a limited capacity on Friday and is set to be available against the Commanders. The All-Pro running back missed two games with a hamstring injury before returning against the Cowboys on Monday night. However, Barkley was limited in the game after reaggravating his hamstring and injuring his back. "I feel decent. Good week of work, rehab, so I feel good to go back out there and practice," Barkley said after practice on Friday. "Being smart, listening to the trainers, listening to the strength guys and the strength staff, and just doing whatever I can to get back on that football field. That's what my motivation is. The team signed Jaydon Blue to the active roster after placing Dameon Pierce on Injured Reserve. Veteran running back Elijah Mitchell was elevated from the practice squad against the Commanders and could be elevated again this week if the Eagles desire three active running backs. Once Pierce exited the game, Mitchell made an impact receiving out of the backfield. Outside linebacker Jonathan Greenard was a full participant at practice while Jalyx Hunt remained limited. With Nolan Smith clearing concussion protocol, the Eagles will have all of their edge rushers available – a rarity this season. Defensive tackle Moro Ojomo was limited in practice all week with a neck injury, but will also be available against the Cowboys. "I feel like the last couple of weeks I've been dealing with different crap and I just want to feel healthy and just go out there and practice with those boys because practice is so important," Ojomo said on Friday. "So that's kind of been a pain, but the trainers have been great about that and coaches have been great about that." Return specialist Britain Covey (knee) has officially been ruled out of Sunday's contest, joining fellow wide receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), both of whom have not practiced for two straight weeks. On the defensive side of the ball, linebacker Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad) and cornerback Jonathan Jones (hamstring) have been ruled out after not participating in practice all week. No players are listed as questionable. Safety Marcus Epps was added to the Eagles' injury report on Thursday with a jaw injury that required a concussion evaluation. He was officially limited in practice. Six players would not have practiced on Wednesday and those same six players did not practice on Thursday: running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back), linebacker Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad), wide receiver/punt returner Britain Covey (knee), cornerback Jonathan Jones (hamstring), wide receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring), and wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks (ankle). home.headline: Commanders' final injury report takes a serious turn along defensive line
home.blurb: Javon Kinlaw missed practice all week, so it wasn't much of a surprise when the Washington Commanders officially listed him as out on their final injury report Friday. The surprise was Daron Payne , who was added with a foot injury; he's officially questionable after being limited in practice on the last day. John Bates, Treylon Burks, and Jer’Zhan Newton were all also listed as questionable for Sunday night's game against Philadelphia. Newton is still in his 21-day practice window as he returns from a pectoral injury ; the Commanders must still activate him before he's eligible. Bates improved from not practicing at all to limited, while Burks went from limited to not practicing , then back to limited on Friday . Commanders head coach Dan Quinn didn't hide how impressed he was with Newton's recovery work Wednesday: "Man, he has worked his ass off." Luke McCaffrey, Charles Omenihu , and Deatrich Wise Jr. were limited Friday but carried no game designation; Omenihu was limited all week with groin/ankle injuries. Nick Allegretti rebounded from missing Thursday's practice by returning as a full participant Friday. Jayden Daniels, Stefon Diggs, and Marcus Mariota all finished the week as full participants and carry no game designation. Philadelphia has its own injury problems , ruling out five players for Sunday night's game, including receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring), Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad), Britain Covey (knee), Jonathan Jones (hamstring), and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle). Cornerback Jakorian Bennett is questionable with a knee injury, while Saquon Barkley was limited Friday with hamstring/back issues but carries no game designation. Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle) and Moro Ojomo (neck) were also limited but have no game designation. Tashan Reed of The Washington Post reported that Payne suffered a significant foot injury during practice and will miss Sunday's game. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo also reported that Payne could be headed to injured reserve, with further testing expected Saturday. home.blurb: The team has been relying on backup quarterback Tanner McKee with Jalen Hurts out for the season, recovering from his diagnosis of deep vein thrombosis in his leg and bilateral pulmonary emboli in his lungs. McKee threw for over 200 passing yards but couldn’t find any receivers in the end zone, as Barkley had the Eagles’ only touchdown all game. Along with that, the Eagles have games against the Seattle Seahawks, San Francisco 49ers, and then a rematch against the Giants to close out their regular season. It’s been a difficult season for the Philadelphia Eagles , who suffered their sixth straight loss Sunday night against the Washington Commanders, 27-10. The loss came with star running back Saquon Barkley attempting to help his team amid his lingering hamstring issue. Along with that, they were still without their starting receivers, DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks, due to injuries. Although their season has been hampered by a series of unfortunate circumstances, including injuries to key players, one Eagles legend still believes in them as a team. Former Eagles quarterback Donovan McNabb recently expressed optimism about Philadelphia’s playoff chances despite the team’s ongoing struggles. More news: Ravens Star Under Fire for What He Said After Lamar Jackson Injury vs Bills “I think we can make the playoffs,” McNabb said while speaking on Sports Radio 94WIP , also adding, “It doesn’t matter what your record is: If it’s nine, seven, or eight. You win in the NFC East, and you get in, and anything can happen.” McNabb was reminded that McKee is currently Philadelphia’s starting quarterback, but he still gave him the benefit of the doubt when it comes to the Eagles salvaging their season. “I would stick with Tanner definitely for the next three weeks and see where that leads us,” the Eagles legend said, adding, “I don’t think there’s a desperate need to make a change now for someone who just got there.” While speaking with Kay Adams for “ Up & Adams with Kay Adams ,” McNabb indicated that he thinks the winner of the upcoming Eagles-Giants Week 9 game will win the NFC East. That game occurs on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 1 p.m. ET in Philadelphia, giving the home team a chance to snap their losing streak. The Eagles are currently 2-6, while the Giants lead the division with a 4-2-1 record. The 3-5 Dallas Cowboys haven’t done themselves any favors when it comes to trying to win the division, as they squandered a home game against the Cardinals on Sunday and lost on a field goal in overtime. Meanwhile, the Commanders improved to 2-4-1 by defeating the Eagles, giving Jayden Daniels and Washington a chance at the division if they can use this momentum. If Philadelphia hopes to win the division and reach the playoffs, it might need to pull off some upsets over some challenging opponents on its remaining schedule. They’ll get a bye week after the Giants game before traveling to Pittsburgh to face Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers on Sunday, Nov. 22. More news: Saquo

home.headline: Eagles at Commanders Injury Report
home.blurb: RB Saquon Barkley against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 7 action After not practicing on Wednesday and Thursday with hamstring and back injuries, Saquon Barkley practiced in a limited capacity on Friday and is set to be available against the Commanders. The All-Pro running back missed two games with a hamstring injury before returning against the Cowboys on Monday night. However, Barkley was limited in the game after reaggravating his hamstring and injuring his back. "I feel decent. Good week of work, rehab, so I feel good to go back out there and practice," Barkley said after practice on Friday. "Being smart, listening to the trainers, listening to the strength guys and the strength staff, and just doing whatever I can to get back on that football field. That's what my motivation is. The team signed Jaydon Blue to the active roster after placing Dameon Pierce on Injured Reserve. Veteran running back Elijah Mitchell was elevated from the practice squad against the Commanders and could be elevated again this week if the Eagles desire three active running backs. Once Pierce exited the game, Mitchell made an impact receiving out of the backfield. Outside linebacker Jonathan Greenard was a full participant at practice while Jalyx Hunt remained limited. With Nolan Smith clearing concussion protocol, the Eagles will have all of their edge rushers available – a rarity this season. Defensive tackle Moro Ojomo was limited in practice all week with a neck injury, but will also be available against the Cowboys. "I feel like the last couple of weeks I've been dealing with different crap and I just want to feel healthy and just go out there and practice with those boys because practice is so important," Ojomo said on Friday. "So that's kind of been a pain, but the trainers have been great about that and coaches have been great about that." Return specialist Britain Covey (knee) has officially been ruled out of Sunday's contest, joining fellow wide receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), both of whom have not practiced for two straight weeks. On the defensive side of the ball, linebacker Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad) and cornerback Jonathan Jones (hamstring) have been ruled out after not participating in practice all week. No players are listed as questionable. Safety Marcus Epps was added to the Eagles' injury report on Thursday with a jaw injury that required a concussion evaluation. He was officially limited in practice. Six players would not have practiced on Wednesday and those same six players did not practice on Thursday: running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back), linebacker Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad), wide receiver/punt returner Britain Covey (knee), cornerback Jonathan Jones (hamstring), wide receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring), and wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks (ankle). home.headline: Eagles-Commanders Final Injury Report: Saquon Barkley WILL play
home.blurb: Barkley returned to practice on Friday — albeit in a limited capacity — after being listed under did not participate on Wednesday and Thursday. There’s no question that Barkley wanting to play and help his team try to turn the season around is admirable. But the team should protect him from himself and sit him down if he’s not nearly healthy enough to play and remain in the game. Which is reasonable to think that’s the case considering he wasn’t even able to fully participate in a practice this week! While overcompensating for his hamstring injury, Barkley injured his back on his first rushing attempt in Week 7 and then played sparingly through obvious discomfort the rest of the game. What’s the point of that? What if he gets further injured? That’s not only a setback as it relates to this season, which very well might be cooked anyway, but potentially long-term as well. It could also prevent teams from making offers not only ahead of the NFL trade deadline but in the offseason, too. Even if you’re not of the mind he should be traded at any point, you should want him healthy for next year! I just think playing him is a short-sighted decision with much more downside than upside. The Eagles ruled five players OUT: DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, Jihaad Campbell, Britain Covey, and Jonathan Jones. Smith and Wicks did not practice this week ahead of their second straight game missed; the Eagles will once again be without their top two wide receivers. With Covey also out, the Eagles only have four healthy wide-outs on the roster: Darius Cooper, Makai Lemon, Hollywood Brown, and Elijah Moore. Against the Cowboys last week, Cooper played the most snaps of any Eagles WR while Lemon was right behind him. Despite this, Cooper only saw three targets while Lemon saw eight. The team will probably look to force-feed their rookie first-round pick again in this matchup. To be determined if they’ll look to elevate a fifth receiver from the practice squad. Their options there: Erik Ezukanma, Xavier Gipson (who also has returning experience), and Quentin Skinner. The Eagles ruled one player QUESTIONABLE: Jakorian Bennett. Bennett fully participated in practice all week. He’s still in his 21-day practice window to return from injured reserve. The Eagles have until 4:00 PM Eastern on Saturday to activate him from IR in order for him to play on Sunday. They’ll need to open a roster spot to do so. Nolan Smith is notably set to return after missing Week 7 due to a concussion. Michael Carter II is also set to return after missing the Eagles’ last two games. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights The Bears take their surging offense into Seattle for a matchup with one of the NFL's best defenses Getty Images In the Week 8 edition of "Monday Night Football," the Seattle Seahawks host the Chicago Bears . Seattle enters this game fresh off a victory over the previously undefeated Kansas City Chiefs , snapping a two-game losing skid. The Seahawks' defense is settling in and once again looks like one of the best units in the league, but faces one of its toughest tests of the season on Monday night. Chicago enters having won both of its games since starting quarterback Caleb Williams returned from injury, improving to 5-2 in the process. The Bears have looked like one of the best offenses in the NFL whenever Williams has been on the field, but they, too, face arguably their toughest test of the season on Monday evening. Will Seattle make it back-to-back wins, or will the Bears ruin their evening with a road upset? How to watch Seahawks vs. Bears live Date: Monday, Nov. 2 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Lumen Field (Seattle) TV: ESPN/ABC | Streaming: Fubo ( try for free ) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Seahawks -3, O/U 46.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Bears have the ball Chicago has scored, 59, 31 and 30 points in the three Caleb Williams starts that were not played against the Minnesota Vikings in a driving rainstorm. The Bears piled up 552, 368 and 405 yards in those three games, and turned the ball over only twice in those contests. For the season (including the game against Minnesota), Williams has completed 71% of his passes at an average of 8.2 yards per attempt, both of which are career-high figures. He has thrown five touchdowns against one interception and rushed 24 times for 128 yards and two additional scores. Williams has generally thrown short passes, with an average depth of throw of only 7.0 yards, according to Tru Media. Despite that, he has created explosive passing plays at the third-highest rate in the league (10.7% of dropbacks). That's thanks in large part to the fact that the Bears are averaging 6.4 yards after catch per completion on his throws, the fourth-best mark in the league. The Seahawks, though, limit YAC as well as just about any team in football. They've allowed only 4.5 yards after catch per completion, which ranks third-best in the NFL. They play shell coverages a lot of the time, and they rally to the ball and tackle as well in the secondary as anybody. Their defensive backs and linebackers rarely miss opportunities to bring ball-carriers to the ground. The Bears generally want to run the ball more often than almost any team in the league, with a 48.7% rush rate, according to Tru Media. The Seahawks are elite at stopping the run, however, as we saw last week against Kenneth Walker III . D'Andre Swift and Roschon Johnson will have their work cut out for them here, even against a defense that plays a lot of nickel and dime and doesn't load the box. The Chicago offensive line will have to do a lot of work to move Seattle's defensive front off the ball, which has proven extremely difficult for opposing lines this year. When the Seahawks have the ball Seattle's offense is built almost entirely around the exploits of superstar wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba . JSN leads the NFL with 867 receiving yards, 43 receiving first downs and eight receiving touchdowns. He has been targeted on 36.3% of the team's pass attempts, which ranks as the No. 1 mark in the NFL. So does his 33.9% targets-per-route-run rate, which is narrowly ahead of CeeDee Lamb's . Smith-Njigba has more receptions than the next three closest players on the Seahawks: AJ Barner , Cooper Kupp and Rashid Shaheed combined for 53. His 867 yards are also considerably more than the 562 that trio has combined as well. They are ancillary pieces at best, and typically they are scarcely involved in the offense. Shaheed is also out on Monday night, which means the secondary options will be even more limited than usual. The Bears, like everyone else in the league, do not have anyone who can cover Smith-Njigba. It's not possible. The best chance to limit him is to get to Sam Darnold and force hurried decisions that lead to turnovers. Darnold, despite missing time due to injury, leads the NFL with eight interceptions. Under pressure, he has been dreadful, completing only 26 of 66 passes for 331 yards, two touchdowns and four picks. He ranks second-to-last in the league in EPA per dropback on pressured plays, per Tru Media. If the Bears can get into his face, they can force him into mistakes and flip the game on its head. Something that will help them in that effort is the arrival of defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons , who is a game wrecker on the interior. Simmons is among the league leaders in both pressures and sacks when lined up inside. He'll have to deal with what is now one of the best guard duos in the league in Quenton Nelson and Grey Zabel , and Simmons could also see his snaps limited in his first game with his new team. (Nelson is likely to play a full complement in his Seattle debut, given how reluctant teams are to rotate offensive linemen.) The Seattle running game should get a boost from the expected returns of Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price . Charbonnet hasn't played all season after tearing his ACL during last year's Super Bowl run, while Price has been out since Week 3 with a chest injury. The combination of Emanuel Wilson and George Holani has largely been ineffective, and even if Charbonnet and Price can generate slightly below-average efficiency, they'll represent an improvement over the incumbent duo. The Bears have given up an average of 4.4 yards per carry this season, which ranks 23rd in the league. Seattle's defense is looking like the unit we expected it to be coming into the year. The Seahawks just shut down Kenneth Walker last week; they should be able to do the same to D'Andre Swift. That puts the entire game on Williams' right shoulder. He can handle that, of course, but it's incredibly difficult to do against Mike Macdonald's unit. That's especially true if the Seahawks get Price and Charbonnet back in the lineup at running back and can run the ball with some degree of success. Pick the Seahawks to take care of business at home. Both of these teams are currently in the wild card mix in the NFC, and while they both want to win their respective divisions, having the tiebreaker in the head-to-head meeting could go a long way for their playoff hopes. Sam Darnold and the Seahawks are coming off a huge win over the Kansas City Chiefs in primetime in Week 7, and they have the No. 2 defense in the NFL in EPA/Play (No. 1 in yards per play allowed) through seven weeks. Meanwhile, the Bears had a mini bye after a Thursday night win in Week 7, and they’re 5-2 overall with three wins in four starts by former No. 1 overall pick Caleb Williams. The Bears star is firmly in the mix to win the MVP award this season, and he’s looking to throw for 300 yards for the third game in a row. Can he make it happen against this elite Seattle defense? Oddsmakers have set the defending champs as favorites at home on Monday night, but the Bears have won and covered in every game that Williams has started and finished this season. In the leadup to Week 8, the SI Betting team has made game picks, player prop selections and more for the Bears vs. Seahawks battle. With so much at stake in this NFC showdown, here’s a compilation of our favorite bets for this matchup on Monday night. Ben Johnson is clearly the real deal as head coach, and Caleb Williams has improved significantly since last season. Last season, he ranked 39th out of 45 starting quarterbacks in completion percentage over expected. This season, he ranks first at +9.0%. The Bears' defense has also been better than people expected this season, ranking fourth in the NFL in opponent success rate. I still have some concerns surrounding the Seattle offense. It did enough to beat the Chiefs last week, but their running game is still weak, and Sam Darnold hasn't been as efficient as he was a year ago. I'll take the Bears as my upset pick of the week. Former first-round pick Rome Odunze has played a big role for the Bears this season, catching 24 of his 38 targets for 381 yards while playing 84.9 percent of the team’s offensive snaps. However, he only has two games this season with more than three receptions, and he’s been targeted seven or fewer times in six of his seven appearances. With that usage, I’m going to fade Odunze on Monday against a Seattle defense that is No. 2 in the NFL in EPA/Pass through seven weeks. Odunze doesn’t have nearly a big enough target share in Ben Johnson’s offense to trust to have one of his best games of the season against this elite defense. With Jaxon Smith-Njigba almost certainly being a player that's going to be targeted early and often in this game, I'm willing to bet on him hauling in at least one pass of 30+ yards. home.blurb: Seahawks’ Week 8 injury report vs. Bears: Zach Charbonnet, Jadarian Price set to return for MNF clash - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Alex House, ClutchPoints Mon, November 2, 2026 at 5:08 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads It is quite easy to blame the Seattle Seahawks ' uneven first half on an inefficient run game, but the defending Super Bowl champions did not exactly post eye-popping numbers on the ground during the 2025 regular season. They averaged 4.1 yards per carry and ranked 11th in the league with 123.3 rushing yards per week. Though, even when the backfield was lacking firepower, it still posed a threat to defenses. The 2026 Seahawks are hoping to get that back on Monday. Emanuel Wilson has done his best to shoulder the burden following Kenneth Walker III's free-agency departure and multiple injuries to the position group, eclipsing 80 rushing yards on three separate occasions. He can use some help, though. An incoming future Hall of Fame offensive lineman like Quenton Nelson should provide a huge boost , but a versatile RB room is an important element of many successful teams. And Seattle (4-3) is ready to shake things up a bit. Zach Charbonnet is expected to make his season debut versus the Chicago Bears , and although he is still on injured reserve at time of print, rookie Jadarian Price is in line to join him. The former is returning from a torn ACL he suffered in the playoffs back in January, and the latter logged full practice participation on Friday after missing the last month of action with a chest injury. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Bears are inserting All-Pro defensive tackle and big midseason acquisition Jeffery Simmons into their front seven, so the Seahawks may have a better chance of keeping Chicago on its toes with their top-three ball-carriers. Fans have seen what quarterback Sam Darnold can accomplish when Seattle establishes its ground attack. Even without Kyle Monangai, who is still battling turf toe and a thumb injury, the Bears boast a dangerous D'Andre Swift-led rushing unit. The Seahawks must close the gap in that crucial area on Monday night. Their chances of doing so have seemingly improved. Opening kickoff will commence at 8:15 p.m. ET.
